national.title: France says Iran behind costly grocery store refrigeration hacks
national.summary: The Paris prosecutor's office says investigators have determined that a cyberattack on grocery store chains was "carried out to serve a foreign power — in this case, Iran."
national.body: French officials believe Iran was behind nationwide cyberattacks on commercial refrigeration units at hundreds of grocery stores in October, the Paris prosecutor's office said Monday, accusing a cyber unit of Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of carrying out the costly hacks. On Tuesday, France's foreign minister said the country "rules nothing out" in its response to what he called "a terrorist organization that has committed an attack of unprecedented scale and aggression against our country." The Oct. 11 hacking attack struck major supermarket chains, hitting "700 retail locations across France," according to the prosecutor's office, which said the attack caused "significant food spoilage and triggered roughly twenty fires" as the temperatures in refrigeration units shot up.The attacks on the French grocery store chains were followed weeks later by similar hacks affecting refrigerators and freezers at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden. A separate cyberattack targeted several blood banks in France, but the products and samples were not damaged.In August, refrigeration outages at six U.S. military bases sparked an ongoing investigation by the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division, Thomas Hamilton, a public affairs officer for the department, told CBS News. Hamilton told CBS News this week that the division's Cyber Field Office was working with French law enforcement to understand the refrigeration outages in Europe. There has been no assertion yet by officials in France, the U.S. or the other European nations hit by the hacks that all of the incidents were connected. national.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
national.summary: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
national.body:
The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi.

While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive".

Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive".

Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario.

Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed.

At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war".

Kushner had said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.

He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting.

national.title: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash
national.summary: The contents of the calendar, including hair clips and keychains, have been widely criticised on social media.
national.body:
Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering customers refunds for its $148 (£110) advent calendar which has been widely criticised on social media.

The accessories advent calendar promised "twelve days of fun surprises" but has been mocked online for the quality of its contents, such as hair clips and keychains, with some comparing them to something you would find down the back of a sofa.

A spokesperson for Skims has told a number of media outlets "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations" and the company has "personally contacted every customer" to offer a full refund or credit to put towards other products".

The shapewear and clothing business was co-founded by Kardashian in 2019 and has made the reality TV star a billionaire, according to Forbes magazine.

Skims was valued at $5bn in 2025 when it raised millions of dollars in new funding.

One account on TikTok called spicychathouse compared the contents of the calendar to things "my cat collects from around my house". Another account said it looked like "a bunch of stuff that Kim Kardashian was emptying out of her bedside table".

A number of accounts showed people cleaning out their own sofas and claiming they had accidentally created the Skims advent calendar.

"It is really interesting to see this kind of backlash," said Kate Vlietstra, senior director of food and drink at market research analyst Mintel.

national.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
national.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
national.body:
Israel's new parliament has been sworn in, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The former army chief has been tasked with forming a government after receiving more recommendations from members of the Knesset than Netanyahu, although not all those backing him are willing to govern together.

Eisenkot's bloc of four parties won 48 seats in October's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.

Almost half of the new MKs did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats.

Shortly after they were sworn in, Netanyahu and Eisenkot warned parliament about the perils of supporting a government led by the other.

"[And] to those who are thinking of establishing a government that includes supporters of terror and haters of Israel, or that will be dependent on them, I ask you, are you prepared to be dependent on those whose goal is the destruction of the Jewish state?" said Netanyahu, alluding to the prospect of an Eisenkot-led government reliant on support from Arab parties.

He also appealed for the formation of a government of national unity as the only way to confront what he said was the threat of "a nuclear Iran".

"I sat and listened to the outgoing prime minister's delusional, divisive, hate-filled and shameful speech, exploiting a state occasion," he said. "I am now even more convinced that he is unfit to remain in office for even one more minute."

Crosetto in September called on the EU to boost security as part of its Aspides mission , the aim of which is to protect commercial shipping from coming under fire by Iran or its Yemeni allies, the Houthi rebels, in the Red Sea and surrounding waters. The Houthis intensified attacks in the Red Sea, targeting Saudi-linked vessels over the summer, in response to Saudi Arabia's backing of Yemeni government forces in the country's decade-long civil war. Crosetto told Reuters that despite the lack of progress, the EU's senior diplomat Kaja Kallas "fully understood" the importance of the request. In September she wrote to the 27 EU member states to ask them to boost their contributions to the initiative. "About one-third of European operations depend on Italy's contribution," said Crosetto. "Other ‌countries, far larger than us, contribute much, much less." "If it is right to invest in missions, then it is right that everyone contributes," he added.

national.title: Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up
national.summary: The BBC gains rare access to a specialist drone unit defending the eastern city of Slovyansk from heavy Russian fire.
national.body:
"If I say run, you run," Tetiana tells us. She and her colleague Yasha are escorting us into a city now under constant bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs.

It is raining and cloudy as we enter the city, and our military escorts call this "good" weather, meaning it is bad for drones.

But the threat is still there, and Yasha keeps his eyes peeled on the skies, while 21-year-old Tetiana scours her phone for the latest military intelligence on likely threats from the air.

They are members of a drone unit who call themselves Peaky Blinders and their distinctive emblem is a flat cap of the type made popular by the cult BBC TV series, although theirs are camouflaged.

Slovyansk is one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control.

Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Ukrainians worry that doing so would make it much easier for Russia to advance further west, including to the capital Kyiv.

Once inside the city, we leave our vehicles hidden under the cover of trees and venture out on foot. Yasha carries a shotgun – a last resort to shoot down Russian drones. In halting English, Tetiana tells us walking is safer than travelling by car.

national.title: Gas prices slip below $4 a gallon for first time since July
national.summary: Petroleum expert Patrick De Haan predicts prices will continue to sink and reach $3.75 a gallon by Thanksgiving.
national.body: Gasoline prices in the U.S. are below $4 a gallon for the first time in nearly four months.According to AAA, the national average for a gallon of gasoline was $3.98 on Tuesday, down from $4.56 a gallon earlier this year.Patrick De Haan, a petroleum expert at tracking firm GasBuddy, predicts that fuel prices will continue to ease into the Thanksgiving holidays.Diesel costs have also fallen, with the national average now running at $6.16 a gallon, down from $6.53 in late September.Why are prices down?Gas prices have fallen in recent weeks as filling stations switch from summer-blend fuels to cheaper winter blends. Federal rules require gas stations to sell a summer blend, designed to guard against evaporation, from June 1 to Sept. 15. Outside that period, stations are allowed to use a winter blend, which is cheaper to produce, explaining why prices often fade in the fall.The switch to the winter blend coincides with a drop in demand, as people take fewer road trips and vacations during the winter months. According to AAA, gas prices fall by around 10 to 30 cents per gallon during the winter months for that reason.Global oil costs, the main factor determining prices at the pump, have also dipped amid hopes that the midterm elections could open the door to a deal between the U.S. and Iran to end the war. On Tuesday, Brent crude, the international benchmark, was trading at around $91 per barrel.In an interview with CBS News "60 Minutes" on Sunday, President Trump said he is "not looking" to escalate the war in Iran."I don't think there's any reason to," he told "60 Minutes" correspondent Ross Douthat.The timeline for reaching a resolution, however, remains unclear. Gregory Brew, senior analyst for Iran and energy for the political risk consultancy Eurasia Group, said Monday that the prospect for a deal remains "unlikely." "Despite ongoing mediation, neither the U.S. nor Iran has shifted its negotiating position," he said in a research note Monday. While gas prices have eased, analysts say the high cost of fuel sparked by the war has spilled into other categories, keeping inflation elevated. October's CPI data, released Tuesday, shows food prices rose at a monthly pace of 0.5% in October after remaining flat in September.

national.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
national.summary: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
national.body:
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.

The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.

In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.

It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.

Published 19 September 2024 Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.

It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".

The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.

The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.

national.title: Twelve dead after motorway pile-ups in Bulgaria fog
national.summary: About 50 other people were injured in the pile-ups along a section of the Trakia motorway, officials have said.
national.body:
Twelve people have been killed after dozens of cars and lorries were involved in two pile-ups on the Trakia motorway in south-eastern Bulgaria, Prime Minister Rumen Radev has said.

Health Minister Katya Ivkova said 11 people died at the scene on Tuesday, near the town of Zimnitsa, while another person later died in hospital. About 50 others were taken to hospital with injuries.

Sliven regional governor Mihail Kasherov told journalists that more than 70 vehicles were involved in the incident, Bulgarian state news agency BTA reported.

Officials have said dense fog reduced visibility and was the likely cause of the first crash, which occurred on the eastbound carriageway.

Radev declared Wednesday a day of national mourning following the incident.

The second crash, on the Sofia-bound carriageway, was likely also caused by the fog, with drivers also distracted by the first crash, BTA reported an official as saying.

The Trakia motorway runs from west-to-east of Bulgaria, and connects the capital Sofia to the Black Sea coast.

Road administration director Galin Kostov added that speeds were unsuitable for the conditions, which included wet road surfaces, and the motorway would remain closed until it had been cleared, BTA reported.

Kaylub Giamanco, 36, was driving by Silver Rail Elementary School on Oct. 15 on his way home for lunch when he saw the shooter, later identified as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, fire at a passing pickup truck with a shotgun. The shooter then forced his way into the school, where Giamanco's two daughters are students. "It was like fight or flight, and something clicked, and I just, I analyzed the situation. I knew something was up. All the emotions flood out of me. I just kind of went into a mission mode," Giamanco said. Giamanco called 911 and said he was following the shooter into the building. He said he then crawled into the building and peeked into the classroom window, where he saw the gunman struggling with a teacher. She was unarmed, but had thrown her cellphone at the shooter and tackled him, according to police. Giamanco said that the teacher's intervention gave him "the split second of having two people side-by-side." "I knew that he wasn't paying attention to me, so it gave me the opportunity to swing the door open and step in and complete my mission, so to speak," Giamanco said. Giamanco said that after he shot the gunman the first time, the shooter was still alive, "struggling with his weapon" and "trying to regain control." The shooter was also trying to say something, Giamanco said, but he didn't listen. "I didn't want to hear what he had to say. He had taken lives," Giamanco said. "I said 'F--- you.'" national.summary: House Republicans will move Tuesday to select their leader in the minority after a brutal drubbing at the polls, with the two candidates being House Majority Leader Steve Scalise of Louisiana and Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan of Ohio.
national.body:
Kevin Freking, Associated Press Kevin Freking, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — House Republicans will move Tuesday to select their leader in the minority after a brutal drubbing at the polls, with the two candidates being House Majority Leader Steve Scalise of Louisiana and Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan of Ohio.

The lawmakers and those set to join the next Congress are gathering in the morning for a vote expected in the afternoon.

WATCH: Hegseth says House impeachment push is about 'policy disagreements' not high crimes

Scalise and Jordan have faced off before, both running to serve as House speaker after Kevin McCarthy was ousted from the job a little more than three years ago. Neither was able to rally the support necessary to secure the position, which eventually went to Mike Johnson, who is stepping aside from the leadership in the new Congress.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Now Republicans are headed into the minority, changing the nature of the job. The winner of the leadership race will inherit a historically small House Republican conference that is only beginning to grapple with its loss of power as President Donald Trump serves out his final two years in office. Leading the party back to the House majority in 2028 is sure to be a stiff climb, given the scope of Democratic victories in the midterms.

Scalise, 61, has held key GOP leadership positions going back to 2014, serving as party whip and then as majority leader. In 2017, he was critically wounded when a gunman opened fire at a baseball practice where several Republican lawmakers and staffers were preparing for an annual charity baseball game against Democrats. In 2023, he was stricken with multiple myeloma, a blood cancer that was successfully treated.

national.title: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
national.summary: The group, formed by Trump, issues rare criticism of Israel, while also blaming Hamas for the suffering of civilians in Gaza.
national.body:
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has called on Israel to immediately allow all necessary humanitarian supplies into Gaza after rain flooded tens of thousands of tents.

The US-backed body, established to oversee the implementation of Trump's Gaza peace plan, acknowledged the steps now being considered by Israel, but said "the response remains insufficient".

Israel's military agency in charge of co-ordinating aid into Gaza said it had allowed in tens of thousands of tents and trucks with winter supplies, but added reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".

On Sunday, three children and a woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in the central Strip.

Most people in Gaza have been displaced because of Israel's military actions. Around 65% of the population, about 1.4 million people, now live in tents or makeshift shelters, the UN says.

Standing soaked in Gaza City, Mohammed Jneid told the AFP news agency that heavy rains hit from one side and sewage overflowed on them from the other, with the ground and tents no longer able to hold.

"We have nothing left, no bedding, no food, nothing," he said.

Sitting inside her tent, Islam Al Mobayed told AFP there were seven children there, five of them young.

national.title: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut
national.summary: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.
national.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month.

It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times.

It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off.

In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year.

Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."

national.title: US inflation higher than expected in October - here's what is happening with prices
national.summary: Prices rose by 0.4% over the month, driven by increases in shelter, food and energy costs.
national.body:
US inflation rose at a faster-than-expected pace in October, according to official figures.

Prices rose by 0.4% in the month, which was lower than the 0.6% increase in September.

However, analysts had expected prices to rise by 0.3%, and the higher-than-expected pace could add to arguments for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next meeting in December.

The new figures come a week after the midterm elections which were fought over cost-of-living pressures across the US.

Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increases over time.

For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%.

Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI).

It tracks the price changes of hundreds of day-to-day items including fresh food, gasoline and medical services to work out the overall level of inflation in the US economy.

national.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
national.summary: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high.
national.body:
Inflation-scarred consumers are finding a bit of relief these days at an unlikely place: the gas pump.

Affordability Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill? The average price of gasoline dipped below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months, according to AAA . The price of regular gas has fallen by 38 cents in the last month to a national average of $3.98.

The overall cost of living, however, remains stubbornly high. Consumer prices in October were up 0.4% from the previous month, according to a report Tuesday from the Labor Department . That's a bigger monthly increase than forecasters had expected.

Rising housing costs accounted for about a third of the monthly increase. Grocery prices were also up sharply during the month.

The drop in gasoline prices in recent weeks is thanks to a combination of falling crude oil prices, refineries' switch to a cheaper blend of winter fuel, and the typical seasonal drop in demand for gas.

"Temperatures are getting colder," says Patrick De Haan, petroleum analyst for GasBuddy. "People who have boats and RVs are probably done for the year. I would say, by Thanksgiving, so long as we don't get any wild cards geopolitically, the national average could be $3.75 a gallon."

Business Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath Gas prices are still at a record high for this time of year, however — about a dollar a gallon higher than when the U.S. went to war with Iran. Even with the recent drop in prices, this year's drive to grandma's for Thanksgiving could be the most expensive ever.

Diesel prices have also fallen, but more slowly than gas prices. AAA says the average price of diesel fuel is $6.15 a gallon, down about 13 cents from a month ago.

national.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
national.summary: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir.
national.body:
FILE - In this photo provided by the North Korean government, its leader Kim Jong Un, center, and his daughter, reportedly named Kim Ju Ae, visit a military training base in North Korea, Thursday, March 19, 2026. Independent journalists were not given access to cover the event depicted in this image distributed by the North Korean government. The content of this image is as provided and cannot be independently verified. 朝鮮通信社/KCNA via KNS via AP hide caption

SEOUL, South Korea — Until she fled North Korea three years ago, Kim Yumi felt deeply frustrated whenever state TV showed leader Kim Jong Un with his young daughter. The message, she felt, was clear and worrying: North Korea was laying the groundwork for an eventual hereditary transfer of power, this time to Kim's daughter.

Publicly questioning the Kim dynasty's hold on power would mean severe persecution. Already angered by draconian pandemic regulations that ruined her family's fishing business, she defected to South Korea by boat with her family.

"My husband and I didn't want our children to live under a fourth-generation dictatorship. As parents, we thought the best thing we could do for our children was to give them freedom," said Kim Yumi, 32, who now lives in Seoul.

North Korea allows no dissent and harshly punishes attempts to flee the country. Established in 1948, the nation is nominally a socialist republic, but in reality it is an authoritarian dynasty, with three generations of the Kim family ruling in succession. There was no known public resistance during its previous two successions — from state founder Kim Il Sung to his son Kim Jong Il in 1994 and then from Kim Jong Il to his son Kim Jong Un in 2011.

This time, North Korea is apparently trying something radical.

Kim Jong Un's repeated public appearances with his daughter over the past four years have led to speculation that she's being groomed as her father's heir.

Asia Kim Jong Un's daughter close to being designated future leader, says spy agency The question of who will become North Korea's next leader is crucial because that person will face a huge challenge — governing an impoverished, nuclear-armed nation whose 26 million people have little political freedom and live under strict state surveillance while being cut off from much of the outside world.

national.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
national.summary: His resignation offer comes amid a widening political rift between Prabowo and Widodo and a separate investigation into allegations that senior police officials wiretapped the president.
national.body:
FILE - Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, left, walks with President Prabowo Subianto after Subianto delivered his State of the Nation Address at the parliament building in Jakarta, Indonesia, Friday, Aug. 14, 2026. Dita Alangkara/AP hide caption

JAKARTA, Indonesia — Indonesia's vice president offered to resign during a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto on Tuesday, according to officials, adding to the turmoil at the highest levels of the country's leadership.

Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, held over two hours of talks with Prabowo, according to State Secretariat Minister Prasetyo Hadi.

It was not immediately clear whether Prabowo accepted the resignation, Hadi told reporters at a news conference at the presidential palace. The president advised Raka to "continue pursuing legal avenues to defend the validity of his academic documents," Hadi said.

As he left his office later in the day, Raka made a brief statement to reporters without addressing the resignation offer.

"I respect all criticism and feedback from the public regarding the developments that are taking place," Raka said. "I do not want the current situation to become a prolonged political controversy."

The resignation offer comes amid growing pressure on Raka over a court dispute involving his academic credentials. It was apparently not related to an ongoing probe into allegations that top police officials, including the president's chief of staff Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, had been involved in a wiretap targeting the president. Three other police generals have also been implicated in the case.

Listyo previously served as national police chief under Widodo, who has not been implicated in the wiretapping investigation.

national.title: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
national.summary: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
national.body:
Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile".

On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression".

He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions.

The French cyber-attacks, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food, were followed by a similar hacks against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.

Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".

He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".

France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.

The Paris prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.

national.title: The average cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. hits a record high: over $51,000
national.summary: Vehicle transaction prices are up to a new record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book — and some buyers are extending their car loans to finance them.
national.body:
The average transaction cost for a new vehicle has reached a record high: $51,109. That's according to a report out today from the Kelley Blue Book, which is part of the analytics firm Cox Automotive.

That's about $500 above the last record , set in December 2025.

Car prices have been stubbornly high for years, especially since the pandemic, mainly driven by supply chain issues. And they've gotten higher recently, in part thanks to tariffs and to buyers flocking to, and car companies making, larger, fancier vehicles.

Yet there's a little good news: Cars are getting more expensive … more slowly .

While that $51,109 figure is an all-time high, that's only up 2.1% in the past year.

"A 2.1% year-over-year increase is actually below inflation," said Erin Keating, an executive analyst at Cox Automotive who co-authored the report. Between 2012 and 2021, cars got 3.4% more expensive a year on average, she continued.

The Kelley Blue Book's transaction cost is based on what people wound up paying for a new vehicle — that means whatever's on the sticker price, plus add-ons for fancier features, and minus any incentives, such as dealer discounts.

Economy Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn Your Money Here's the latest sticker shock: Borrowing for a mortgage — or a car It also doesn't include one other expense that adds to the cost of owning a car: interest on auto loans. The cost of borrowing has risen over the past several years as the Federal Reserve has kept interest rates high in an effort to drive down inflation. Auto loan rates are now about 11% for used vehicles and over 7% for new ones, according to Edmunds , a car analytics company.

national.title: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
national.summary: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.
national.body:
One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters.

After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir.

With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces.

President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans.

"She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media.

Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France, Solange Alexandre, née Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One.

"My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917. The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood," she recalled in her memoirs.

In June 1940 she heard on the radio the appeal from General Charles de Gaulle in London, calling on the French not to give up the struggle against Germany. She had never heard of him, but that did not matter.

national.title: California police investigate after 27 fall ill at half-marathon running event
national.summary: A local hospital says runners had "unusual" symptoms after racing on an atypically hot day.
national.body:
Police in Santa Barbara, California, are investigating after nearly 30 people had to seek medical care at a half-marathon running event held in the city on Sunday.

In a statement provided to the BBC's US partner CBS News, officers said they received a report from Santa Barbara Cottage Hospital about race participants who sought medical treatment "for unusual symptoms" after the race ended.

"The cause of the reported symptoms has not been confirmed," the statement added.

Cottage Health, which operates the hospital, told CBS it had seen "a larger than expected number of emergency visits" from those who ran the race.

"There is no specific action recommended for the public at this time; however, participants who feel unwell should seek medical attention and follow guidance from healthcare professionals," police said.

Cottage Hospital said it treated 27 people from the half marathon at emergency rooms in Santa Barbara and the nearby city of Goleta.

The vast majority of them - 24 - were discharged after treatment, while three people were still in hospital as of Monday in stable condition.

Several thousand people ran the half marathon on a hotter-than-usual day in Santa Barbara along the Pacific Ocean. Temperatures reportedly reached 86F (27C) by midday, compared to a typical early November temperature of low 70s.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dug in for a fight Tuesday against his potential impeachment in Congress, telling reporters that a rogue lawmaker is targeting him over "policy disagreements" and not the high crimes or offenses the nation's founders intended.

national.body:
What would it mean to become Miss Ghana 1986? Fame, fortune, perhaps rubbing elbows with '80s superstar Bobby Brown? For a group of six teenage girls at the Aburi Girls Boarding School, the answer is: everything.

The battle for the crown is at the heart of School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play , written by Tony Award-nominated playwright Jocelyn Bioh. The play is ending a Broadway run this week and celebrating with livestream broadcasts on The League of Live Stream Theater's website for a fee (but is free for high schoolers).

School Girls is set at a boarding school in Ghana in 1986. It follows Paulina, the school's queen bee and her crew, whom she frequently belittles and bullies over their looks.

"So, do you want to be fat-fat? Or fit? And popular." Paulina asks Nana, harassing her over eating porridge instead of an apple at lunch.

Ahead of a visit from a pageant recruiter to the school, Paulina's plans to win Miss Ghana go awry after a new transfer student arrives: Ericka from … Ohio!

Ericka exposes Paulina's toxic behavior and shows her up during a performance of Whitney Houston's Greatest Love of All . Ericka, being lighter-skinned than Paulina, sparks a clash between the school's headmistress and the pageant director over beauty and who would have the best chance of winning the Miss Global Universe pageant.

Paulina becomes the victim of circumstances that she cannot control.

School Girls explores the themes of girlhood and impossible societal beauty standards with humor and humanity.

national.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
national.summary: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement.
national.body:
Late Monday, The Associated Press determined that California voters had rejected Prop 40, the proposed billionaire wealth tax I wrote about last week . Given the big blue wave we saw during the midterms, why did this tax on billionaires fail to surf to victory?

To make sense of the results, I went back to the two economists I spoke with last week: UC Berkeley's Gabriel Zucman, a leading champion of wealth taxes, and Stanford's Joshua Rauh, a prominent critic of Prop 40.

Last week, they disagreed on what this wealth tax on billionaires would do to California's economy and tax revenue. Now comes the sequel, in which they disagree on what the results say about the politics of wealth taxes.

Their debate could foreshadow a bigger one in the next Democratic presidential primary: should the party embrace a wealth tax?

Zucman blames the corrosive influence of money for Prop 40's failure.

"I am not surprised," Zucman says. Opponents of Prop 40 spent almost $400 million fighting it, including spending on competing ballot measures, making it one of the most expensive ballot initiative fights in history.

"The money spent by the billionaires was critical," Zucman says. "Anyone who lives in California has been carpet-bombed by a deluge of ads. One can easily see how this could be pivotal in such a closely contested ballot."

But didn't Democrats win plenty of races this cycle despite huge sums spent against them? In Texas, for example, Elon Musk alone poured more than $150 million into defeating Democrat James Talarico. And Talarico ended up winning his Senate race by a comfortable margin . Why would money have been so decisive with Prop 40 and not in other races around the nation?

national.body:
A police officer has died and another has been injured in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo after an explosive device went off at the scene of a shooting.

The blast happened when officers from Spain's canine unit and explosives disposal unit arrived and examined a suspicious backpack following reports of a dispute between neighbours on Tuesday morning .

A woman who had been shot and the injured officer have been taken to hospital for treatment.

The suspect fled the scene and is still at large, police said.

Spanish police paid tribute to the dead officer, who has been named as Juan José, in a statement on X and said: "Our hearts are with his family, friends, colleagues and loved ones."

Officers attended the scene early after receiving reports of an argument between neighbours and upon arriving found a woman who had sustained gunshot wounds, police spokesman Pedro Aguado said.

While searching for the suspected attacker, officers found a suspicious backpack with a flashing light and contacted both the bomb disposal unit and canine unit.

"While the package was being moved outside to ensure the safety of the residents, an explosion occurred," Aguado added.

Israeli forces have shot dead a 14-year-old Palestinian boy during an operation in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say.

The Israeli military said soldiers identified "several terrorists who intended to hurl stones" in an area where stones had previously been thrown at Israeli vehicles. The soldiers fired towards them "to remove the threat", it added.

The Palestinian Red Crescent said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds, but that Israeli forces blocked their access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.

Moataz Daghlas's relatives said Israeli authorities were withholding his body.

Meanwhile, Palestinian news agency Wafa identified the two Palestinians wounded during the raid as a 17-year-old child, who it said was shot in the abdomen and pelvis, and a 19-year-old man, who was shot in the hand.

According to the UN, at least 98 Palestinians, including 22 children, have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year.

Six Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians in the West Bank over the same period, it says.

Ukraine invasion — explained Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections Hopes of ending Europe's biggest conflict since World War II are tempered by the absence of any significant breakthroughs in three previous rounds of talks earlier this year.

Moscow also is seeking to break Ukrainians' will as winter sets in by ramping up its battering of the country's power grid.

national.body: Geneva — The United States is set on Tuesday to become the first country to fully shun a regular review of its human rights record at the U.N.'s top rights body since it was created two decades ago.The Trump administration last year pulled the U.S. out of the Human Rights Council, accusing it of an anti-U.S. and anti-Israel bias, and alleging that it didn't uphold the very values it promotes. Supporters back the council's mandate to keep tabs on human rights in all U.N. member states including the U.S., which has drawn criticism for its policies including strong-arm deportations and targeted killings of alleged drug-runners in the Caribbean and Pacific — which the administration has said are designed to protect U.S. workers and help keep the country safe. The Geneva-based council regularly examines the rights records of all 193 U.N. member states — generally about every four to five years — as part of a process known as the universal periodic review. The United States, under President Trump, already skipped its appointment for its review a year ago. The scheduled November 2025 review was pushed back until Tuesday in hopes that the U.S. government might change its mind. It did not. "(W)e give no credibility to the agency," a State Department spokesperson said in an email to The Associated Press. "This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own 'values' as it pushes anti-American rhetoric," the spokesperson said, alleging the council has a "persistent failure to condemn the most egregious human rights violators." Democrats have won at least 47 of the 63 seats in the state Senate, with one race in the Capital Region still uncalled. They have won at least 111 of the 150 seats in the Assembly. That gives the party the largest Assembly majority in history, and its largest Senate majority in more than a century. With supermajorities in both chambers, they have enough votes to override any potential vetoes from Gov. Kathy Hochul.

Sen. Shelley Mayer, D-Yonkers, who led the party’s Senate campaign efforts, said the new numbers will give the chamber more heft in budget negotiations and on other policy matters, but the diversity of the conference’s membership is a bigger benefit.

"I think our conference will flex its muscles in the budget negotiations," Mayer told the New York Public News Network, though not singling out any particular issue. "The suburbs, the city of New York, the upstate cities, the rural communities, we got to care about it all. And we're going to be able to because we're going to have such broad representation."

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District, finished rehabilitation of the outer breakwater at Dunkirk Harbor on Oct. 19, strengthening critical infrastructure that protects the harbor and the surrounding community from
local.body:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District, completed rehabilitation of approximately 2,300 linear feet of the outer breakwater at Dunkirk Harbor in Dunkirk, New York, on Oct. 19, 2026. The federally funded project strengthens the breakwater against wave and ice damage, improves structural stability, and ensures safe navigation and long-term reliability of the harbor. Photo by Kaylee Wendt

An important project to preserve the Dunkirk Harbor has been completed.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District, finished rehabilitation of the outer breakwater at Dunkirk Harbor on Oct. 19, strengthening critical infrastructure that protects the harbor and the surrounding community from Lake Erie’s powerful waves and ice.

The federally funded project repaired approximately 2,300 linear feet of the 2,800-foot structure, addressing deterioration caused by years of exposure to harsh Great Lakes conditions. The improvements are designed to enhance structural stability, support safe navigation and extend the service life of the breakwater.

Completing this project is another important step in our commitment to maintaining safe and reliable navigation throughout the Great Lakes," said Lt. Col. Aaron Anderson, commander of the USACE Buffalo District. "By investing in critical infrastructure like the Dunkirk Harbor breakwater, we’re protecting these waterways for the communities, businesses and recreational boaters who depend on them."

Originally constructed in 1931, the outer breakwater serves as a protective barrier between the open waters of Lake Erie and Dunkirk Harbor. Over time, wave action and seasonal ice contributed to the deterioration of the structure, creating a need for significant rehabilitation.

The project was completed in two phases by the Corps of Engineers' Michigan-based contractor, Great Lakes Dock and Materials. The first phase addressed approximately 1,850 linear feet of the breakwater under an $8.5 million contract, partially funded through congressionally directed spending. The second phase addressed the remaining 450 linear feet under a $4.5 million contract funded through the fiscal year 2025 workplan.

Construction included placing a stone overlay, known as a rubble mound, along the lakeside of the breakwater, raising its crest elevation two feet above the original design and reinforcing the eastern end of the structure.

local.body:
An explosive water main break in Fredonia Sunday night sent debris flying, damaging at least two vehicles.

Mayor Michael Ferguson told the OBSERVER that the 12-inch line near Gardner and Johnston streets was repaired around 4:30 a.m. Monday morning. The village Department of Public Works got help on the job from S. St George Enterprises.

However, when the high-pressure line failed Sunday night, "it made a pretty big hole," Ferguson said. "It blew about a five-foot hole in the ground."

A photo submitted to the OBSERVER shows a geyser shooting high up into the air from the rupture.

Ferguson acknowledged that at least two, possibly three, parked vehicles in the area were damaged by debris when the rupture blew rocks out of the ground.

The mayor said there was also localized street flooding toward Ventura Circle, and several basements in the vicinity were flooded.

Ferguson said there was no damage to the village's overall water system. "We reacted as soon as we saw the water drop," he said.

"It was just a very high-pressure line that decided to go," he concluded.

local.title: Pomfret switch boosts city water
local.summary: Dunkirk is thirsty for more revenue, and a significant switchover of Pomfret town water customers will moisten its parched lips. Homes and businesses in Pomfret east and south of the Routes 20 and 60 roundabout were switched over to the North County Water District, and taken off Fredonia’s water sys
local.body:
Dunkirk is thirsty for more revenue, and a significant switchover of Pomfret town water customers will moisten its parched lips.

Homes and businesses in Pomfret east and south of the Routes 20 and 60 roundabout were switched over to the North County Water District, and taken off Fredonia's water system, Friday. The city of Dunkirk water plant on Lake Shore Drive is the NCWD's sole supplier.

City Department of Public Works Director Randy Woodbury mentioned the change at a Monday meeting of the Common Council Finance Committee.

"That will be extra income for the city of Dunkirk," he said.

Officials originally intended to do the switchover Jan. 1, Woodbury said. However, Chautauqua County Health Department officials evidently pushed for an early switch amid the Fredonia water treatment plant's recent problems. The village had boil and conservation orders on water in recent weeks.

Woodbury said the county wanted to lessen the production load for the Fredonia plant. The actual process of the switchover took about 15 minutes, he said. "We're making plenty of water to do it," he added.

The area switched over is growing, and "it's quite a chunk of real estate now on Dunkirk water," Woodbury said.

Councilwoman Natalie Luczkowiak asked if the added revenue was in the city's proposed 2027 budget. Woodbury pointed out that was unlikely as no one knew the move would be made early until Friday.

local.title: Bills pull away from Vikings on MNF 23-6
local.summary: MINNEAPOLIS — Josh Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before halftime, James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and the Buffalo Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into their unrelenting offensive slump. Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Do
local.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Josh Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before halftime, James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and the Buffalo Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into their unrelenting offensive slump.

Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams had interceptions and Tyler Bass made four field goals to stretch his franchise-record streak to 25 straight as the Bills (7-1) matched their best eight-game start since 1993. That season ended with their last of four straight Super Bowl losses.

With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz started at quarterback for the Vikings (6-2) and didn’t finish what became one of the worst performances of his 11-year career. Wentz went 8 for 25 for 81 yards and three turnovers, including a backward pass in the first quarter that was thrown too high for even Justin Jefferson to catch it -- resulting in a lost fumble near midfield.

Wentz, who was checked out in the medical tent at one point for an apparent lower leg injury, was replaced by Max Brosmer midway through the fourth quarter. Wentz completed 1 of 8 passes in the second half.

The battle of Buffalo’s highest-scoring offense in the league against the least-scored-on defense might well have gone to Minnesota had the offense been able to muster a decent drive or two.

But the Vikings had four straight possessions in the first half start beyond their 40-yard line, and the furthest they made it was the Bills 48.

The Vikings as usual sent blitzers at Allen from every angle possible, recording four sacks and an interception of a heave into the end zone that Byron Murphy ran down and returned 55 yards. But the Bills eked out just enough in the first half to give themselves a cushion, when Allen found tight end Keleki Latu open in the back of the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown as he rolled right and was hit hard by Andrew Van Ginkel.

With 322 regular-season touchdowns -- 232 passing, 88 rushing and two receiving -- Allen tied Peyton Manning for the most in NFL history over a player’s first 10 years. Allen is halfway through his ninth season.

local.body:
Detroit Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle won the American League Rookie of the Year award and Cincinnati Reds slugger Sal Stewart took home the National League honor Monday night.

McGonigle -- who played most of the season at just 21 years old -- had a .278 batting average and .806 OPS with 18 homers, 72 RBIs, 28 doubles and 12 stolen bases while splitting time between third base and shortstop. He’s the first Tigers player to win the award since pitcher Michael Fulmer in 2016 and the first Tigers infielder since Lou Whitaker in 1978.

The Tigers thought enough of McGonigle’s potential that they signed him to a $150 million, eight-year deal in April, just a few weeks into his rookie season. He backed up that confidence with a stellar all-around season that earned him an All-Star nod and helped the Tigers remain in the playoff race for much of the summer.

Stewart was a force in the middle of the Reds’ lineup with 32 homers and 112 RBIs while playing in all 162 games, including 161 starts. He’s the ninth Reds player to win the award and first since infielder Jonathan India in 2021.

McGonigle received 28 of 30 first-place votes and finished with 204 points in balloting by the Baseball Writers’ Association of America conducted before the postseason.

The other two AL finalists were Cleveland Guardians left-hander Parker Messick and Boston Red Sox lefty Payton Tolle. Messick came in second, earning the other two first-place votes and 122 points after going 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA and 193 strikeouts.

Tolle was third with 54 points. He had a 9-6 record with a 3.03 ERA and 171 strikeouts.

Stewart was selected first on 20 of 30 ballots and finished with 170 points.

local.summary: A 7 News investigation found Buffalo Police overtime hours used to meet minimum staffing jumped 65% in a year, with new officers not expected until 2028.
local.body: The Buffalo Police Department doesn't have enough police officers to cover its own contracted minimum staffing levels, forcing a steep rise in the overtime hours needed to keep patrols staffed and 911 calls answered.That's the central finding of my months-long investigation. After filing a Freedom of Information request to the city, I confirmed the BPD is understaffed to the point where it's relying on overtime to meet basic policing needs. And the problem is only going to get worse before it gets better.My FOIL request asked for the number of overtime hours officers are working to cover contracted minimum staffing levels, known as minimum manpower overtime hours.Fiscal Year 2025 to 2026 saw officers undertake 35,526 minimum manpower overtime hours total, a 65% increase on the previous year. That isn't special detail overtime, such as policing Chippewa St. nightlife or the Saint Patrick's Day Parade, but those hours cover the basics such as responding to 911 calls."I'm not going to make light of the situation. We need to hire officers," said Buffalo Police Commissioner Erika Shields. "We inherited this and we are pushing the timeline as aggressively as possible and I sincerely hope we can get officers on board."Some of the minimum manpower overtime hours are covered on a voluntary basis, and sometimes officers are forced to cover the shifts."I don't know that the department needs to be larger than its authorized strength but what I can say is that we definitely need more officers at the rank of police officer," Shields explained.WATCH: 'Crisis mode': Buffalo Police relying on overtime to meet minimum staffing needsThe last time the city administered a police exam for new recruits was in 2023, and Shields says the subsequent three-year pause caused the problem. "There should have been a hiring exam two years ago," Shields said. "And if not two years ago, absolutely last year because there's such a lag time between administering an exam and getting [officers] on the street, you can't wait until you're in a crisis mode."Under previous administrations, the city created and administered its own police exam for $300,000, according to Shields. entertainment.summary: Kelly Clarkson's daughter is spreading her wings and learning to fly above the drama. As her and late ex-husband Brandon Blackstock's 12-year-old daughter River Rose experiences the ups and downs...
entertainment.body:
Kelly Clarkson 's daughter is spreading her wings and learning to fly above the drama.

As her and late ex-husband Brandon Blackstock's 12-year-old daughter River Rose experiences the ups and downs of junior high school, the Voice coach shared how she took a chance, made a change and guided the tween to break away from the woes of adolescence. nice

"I'm a pretty progressive parent, so I'm like, 'No, no. You're gonna make your own mistakes, and that's OK,'" Clarkson told E! News' Will Marfuggi in an exclusive interview on The Voice season 30 live show red carpet on Nov. 9. "I'm not like an 'I told you so,' but I do implement advice."

"They're growing up," she continued. "One's in junior high, and junior high sucks. It's a hard age with friends, and arguing and stuff like that. I do offer advice, and I've had my daughter come back and be like, 'So you were right.'"

But the 44-year-old— also mom to 10-year-old son Remington Alexander with Blackstock—will always help her daughter stand a little taller, even when she doesn't heed her mom's warnings.

As she explained, "I've had them be like, 'OK, so I didn't do that, and I should have.'"

While Clarkson is hitting all the right notes of motherhood, she's also had a pitch-perfect time on The Voice alongside fellow coaches Adam Levine , Queen Latifah and Riley Green .

Although the Maroon 5 frontman took home gold last season with Alexia Jayy , he couldn't wait another minute to focus on this season.

entertainment.title: Lanterns Co-Showrunner Reacts To DC Studios Shakeup Amid Season 2 Uncertainty
entertainment.summary: Lanterns co-showrunner Chris Mundy has offered his take on the shocking reshuffle at DC Studios, with James Gunn and Peter Safran stepping down as CEOs.
entertainment.body:
John Johnson/HBO Max Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Lanterns" co-showrunner Chris Mundy has offered his take on the shocking reshuffle at DC Studios while there are still questions over a potential second season of the HBO show. Co-chiefs James Gunn and Peter Safran confirmed they were stepping down from their roles in a statement posted to Instagram, with Gunn saying he disliked the "at-times corporate nature of the job."

Many have already wondered whether "Lanterns" Season 2 was on the cards or not, and Mundy touched on it when speaking to The Playlist , also noting Skydance's recent purchase of Warner Bros. "We thought everything had settled [after the merger]," he explained. "I can imagine a world where everyone retreats to their corners, but then, you know, it's a coin flip, 50/50." Mundy's comments don't sound overly positive about the possibility of more ring-slinging action for the Green Lantern Corps on HBO.

"Lanterns" Season 1 ends as John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) finally gets a ring and a power-battery of his own. But he specifically becomes Earth's protector and leaves the rest of the cosmic Sector 2814 in the safe(ish) hands of Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion). It's a way of positioning Stewart into a powerful new place ahead of his role in Gunn's 2027 "Superman" follow-up, "Man of Tomorrow."

John Johnson/HBO Max "Lanterns" was incredibly successful on HBO, with over 10 million viewers tuning in for the finale in October. So it's only natural that audiences want to know if Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler will return for a new mystery adventure on HBO in the future. But a second season was unclear even before the DC Studios reshuffle, and there was already one major condition for its return: The story had to be worth it.

Peter Safran said that was the single deciding factor for the show's future, telling Collider , "If we're able to come up with what we believe to be a worthy successor to a beloved and great first season, that's what's going to dictate whether there's a second season." It's a valid point, since there are plenty of TV shows that should have just ended after one season .

But it seems like the entire creative team shares the same perspective, as co-creator Damon Lindelof told The Daily Beast , "Nobody wants to do it just because the first season was successful. That is to say, everyone's approaching it with the point of view of, should there be a second season? Is the creative worthy of a second season?" For now, "Lanterns" Season 2 seems unlikely, but stranger things have happened. The more pressing issue is whether Skydance chooses to hit reboot on the DC Universe entirely after Safran and James Gunn's exit. Only time will tell.

entertainment.title: Netflix Launches New Brand Advertising Campaign In Engagement Push
entertainment.summary: The streaming giant launched the campaign, 'Find The Thing You Never Knew You Needed,' in the U.S., Canada, Brazil and Spain.
entertainment.body:
As Netflix prepares to overhaul its film and TV offerings under new content chief Peter Rice, the streaming giant is launching a new brand campaign to try and persuade its users to keep tuning in.

The campaign, with the tagline “Find the thing you never knew you needed,” launched Tuesday in the U.S., Canada, Brazil and Spain.

The three spots are each structured like a film (and shot on 35mm!), and each feature a main character in the form of an astronaut, a vampire and an axolotl (an amphibian native to Mexico), with an epic story that culminates in them finding their next show on Netflix.

The campaign comes as Netflix is at an inflection point with its content, with Rice expected to reset its strategy and focus more on the U.S.-Canada market. The change at the top in content came as Netflix’s engagement has not been as strong as it has liked, something that co-CEO Ted Sarandos has talked about publicly.

“People come to Netflix trusting they’ll discover something new to love, often something they didn’t see coming,” said Aarti Thiagarajan, senior director of brand creative studio for Netflix. “We wanted to celebrate that moment when you get hooked. So we started with the things real fans do, like staying up for one more episode or blowing up the group chat about a new obsession, and turned them into a campaign as entertaining as the shows and films that inspire them. Because once you find the thing you never knew you needed, it’s hard to imagine life without it.”

The streamer is also launching a social series called Typecast, featuring creators Willy Chavarria, Teezo Touchdown, Isamaya Ffrench and The Compton Cowboys discussing heir favorite Netflix shows.

Tuesday is new Billboard chart day each week! As all charts update each Tuesday, here’s a look at highlights of the latest rankings dated Nov. 14 and reflecting the Oct. 30-Nov. 5 measurement week, according to data tracker Luminate.

Jackson appears in the charts’ top two simultaneously for the first time since January 1992, when “Black or White” was in its seventh and last week atop the Hot 100 and parent album Dangerous ranked at No. 2 following four weeks leading the Billboard 200. Thriller is also No. 1 on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums for a milestone 40th week, while the title cut, thanks to Halloween play, roars to the top of both Streaming Songs and Digital Song Sales for the first time.

entertainment.title: How Nick Cannon Really Feels About Mariah Carey Prenup
entertainment.summary: Boy, if you wanna know whether Nick Cannon and Mariah Carey had a prenup—he’ll tell you. Ten years after the former couple—who share 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe—finalized their divorce,...
entertainment.body:
Boy, if you wanna know whether Nick Cannon and Mariah Carey had a prenup—he’ll tell you.

Ten years after the former couple—who share 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe —finalized their divorce, the former America’s Got Talent host confirmed they “absolutely” signed a prenuptial agreement before tying the knot in 2008.

“Mariah Carey, her entity, her global conglomerate, is gonna make sure she is protected,” Cannon explained during a Nov. 9 appearance on the On Par with Maury Povich podcast . “Had no problem with it whatsoever. And when it was all said and done, I think it protected both of us.”

Although their divorce wasn’t finalized for two years following their 2014 breakup, the 46-year-old—dad to 10 additional children with five different women—said the process felt “easy.”

Nevertheless, it’s not a process Cannon sees himself going through again, as he doesn’t see himself ever getting remarried.

“I think because of some of the natures of, like, unmarrying are not good,” he continued. “And it’s just the process—you don’t realize it takes so long and how draining it is.”

And while divorce “didn’t affect” his friendship with Carey, he saw how divorce creates pressure points in relationships.

“It really could have affected how we handled one another as friends,” he admitted. “I saw the traps of how this could have turned really bad if we didn’t step in and really engage as a family.”

entertainment.title: Latin Grammy Awards 2026 Predictions: Who Will Win the Top Honors?
entertainment.summary: Billboard 's Latin and Español editors offer an analysis of the likely winners and deserving contenders across the top four categories.
entertainment.body:
Who will win the top prize at the 2026 Latin Grammys ? Every year, Billboard Latin and Billboard Español editors dissect the top categories — album of the year, song of the year, record of the year and best new artist — to forecast the winners and spotlight the most deserving artists.

With the ceremony just around the corner this Thursday (Nov. 12), our editorial team has engaged in an analysis, considering market trends and historical voting patterns to make informed predictions. This discussion includes insights from Sigal Ratner-Arias , deputy editor of Billboard Español ; Jessica Roiz , associate editor for Latin; and Ingrid Fajardo , senior social media manager and staff writer.

On its 26th annual edition, the Latin Grammy Awards ceremony will broadcast live from the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. The three-hour telecast will be produced by TelevisaUnivision and air across the network’s U.S. platforms, beginning at 8 p.m. ET. It will be preceded by the Latin Grammy Premiere, where the majority of the categories are awarded.

To refresh your memory, here’s this year’s full list of nominees . Below are our predictions for the general categories:

Jessica Roiz: All are great works, but the clear winner in my book is Milo J’s La Vida Era Más Corta. In 15 songs, the then 18-year-old bridged the past, present and future, most notably with his star-studded collaborations that include Trueno, Akriila, Silvio Rodríguez and the late Mercedes Sosa. Showcasing the maturity beyond his years, the Argentine artist — who’s one of the youngest to be nominated in this coveted category — beautifully captures Latin America’s rich folk traditions, where chacareras, zambas, chamamés and tangos effortlessly coexist.

Sigal Ratner-Arias: I agree that all of these are excellent and that Milo — despite his young age — has created a truly extraordinary album. However, I don’t see any other winner here besides Rosalía for LUX , a complex, one-of-a-kind masterpiece. Recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra and featuring songs musically and lyrically rich — in 13 different languages! — Rosalía not only expanded the meaning of what a pop album can be, she also reached new vocal heights with an impressive operatic work.

Ingrid Fajardo: I agree with Jessica and Sigal; we definitely saw masterpieces in this category, including Milo J’s La Vida Era Más Corta and Carín León’s MUDA . But Rosalía took us into her world with LUX . For me, it’s a work of art; it feels like reaching the deepest part of her musical thoughts, her knowledge and the art she carries inside, captured in this 18-track album combining a masterful symphony orchestra perfectly intertwined with pop that makes you feel the performance of each song.

entertainment.title: 5 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
entertainment.summary: Looking for more shows like Cyberpunk: Edgerunners after watching Season 2? These five shows explore similar themes of corporate greed and alienation.
entertainment.body:
Studio Trigger/Netflix Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners" Season 2 has recently landed, and while the season is receiving great reviews, it's just as brief as the first. The series dives deep into corporate greed, individuality, resistance, alienation, the ethics of artificial augmentation, and more. These themes are a staple in the increasingly popular cyberpunk genre. It is also quite a feat that a series as short and self-contained became one of the most emotionally charged rollercoasters the genre has to offer.

The neon-drenched landscape, unique character designs, and full-throttle action propelled the show to become one of Netflix's best animated series , and although Rafał Jaki's series is one-of-a-kind, there are a few shows that can offer a similar viewing experience. While these recommendations might not be perfectly in line with the charm of the hit anime, they offer interesting perspectives on the same themes or even share distinct elements of its world.

HBO "Westworld" is a dystopian show set in the cruel Westworld amusement park, which is inhabited by humanoid androids called hosts. The park's management allows wealthy visitors to come in and indulge their fantasies on the hosts with no repercussions. The hosts are programmed to have their memories routinely erased and subjected to a cycle of never-ending violence. Dolores Abernathy (Evan Rachel Wood), one of the hosts, gains consciousness and begins questioning the system in place, setting off events that lead to a full-on insurrection from her kind.

While "Westworld" has the same focus on artificial intelligence as "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," the most interesting similarities lie deeper. Both shows examine the commodification of people and their being exploited by the wealthy. And just like "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," "Westworld" follows its protagonists as they realize the true depravity of their circumstances before deciding to fight back for their survival.

"Westworld" focuses on literal androids rather than humans, but the underlying connection of corporate exploitation and the desire to rebel is something that viewers will deeply empathize with. It also examines the philosophical fine line that divides humans and artificial intelligence, a theme that is baked into the best TV shows the cyberpunk genre has to offer .

Apple TV "Pluribus" stars Rhea Seehorn as successful yet grumpy novelist Carol Sturka , who has her life upended when an extraterrestrial virus breaks out and infects nearly everyone on Earth. This virus joins everyone into a shared collective being and turns the victims into a happy and cooperative consciousness. As Carol grapples with the reality of the world and tries to investigate the full picture, she meets up with other survivors and tries to concoct a plan that will undo the virus and restore the world order.

entertainment.title: Russell Brand’s Ex-Girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith Accuses Him of ‘Violence, Coercive Control and Abuse’
entertainment.summary: TV producer also explains why she took out an order against a masseuse who'd levied claims against Brand
entertainment.body:
Jemima Goldsmith, a woman whom the BBC describes as a TV producer who dated Russell Brand for around a year in 2014, wrote an in-depth description on Monday of ways she alleges Brand inflicted “violence, coercive control and abuse” on her during the relationship on social media . Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault in the U.K. earlier in the day. “I am glad and relieved that Russell Brand has finally faced justice,” she wrote.

What she said of Brand’s alleged abuse, though, constituted the following paragraph: “I had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident,” she wrote. “I chose not to press charges at the time and not to go public with this, as I was worried about the impact of the press attention on my then teenage children. I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014.”

The majority of her post was her account of what she claimed happened surrounding accusations made by masseuse Szilvia Berki of physical assault against Brand concerning an incident that Berki alleged took place in 2014. Berki had claimed that Goldsmith had hired her to give Brand a massage for his birthday. Brand, Berki said, treated her “like a prostitute.”

A judge in 2023 sided with Brand on the matter, and Goldsmith’s account on social media backs him up. “I did not see anything untoward, despite the fact that he was later found guilty of sexually assaulting other women and he later physically assaulted me,” she wrote. “If I saw any man abuse any woman under any circumstances, I would do my utmost to stop them, without hesitation.” She added, “According to the police, at no time did Ms. Berki ever state to them that she had been assaulted, threatened or falsely imprisoned.”

entertainment.title: See Bruce Springsteen Finally Play Western Stars Songs in Public
entertainment.summary: He also told dirty jokes at the annual Stand Up For Heroes charity show, which raised nearly $6 million for veterans groups and their families
entertainment.body:
It’s been seven years since Bruce Springsteen released his acclaimed orchestral pop record Western Stars , but he’s never played any of the songs at a public concert despite all the touring he’s done in that time. That finally changed Monday evening when he performed his annual acoustic set at the Stand Up For Heroes benefit concert at New York City’s David Geffen Hall. The show included the Western Stars songs “Hello Sunshine” and “Moonlight Motel,” in addition to 2007’s “I’ll Work for You Love” and “Dancing in the Dark.”

In keeping with the grand tradition of Stand Up For Heroes, which is organized by the Bob Woodruff Foundation and has raised $123 million for veterans and their families over the past 20 years, Springsteen sprinkled dirty jokes throughout his set. (The show also included performances by Josh Johnson, Hasan Minhaj, the Resilient, Jon Stewart, and Alex Warren.)

“Guy goes into the library,” Springsteen deadpanned to the crowd. “Goes up to the librarian. He goes, ‘Ma’am, do you have a book on small penises?’ She goes, ‘I don’t think it’s in yet.’ ‘Yeah, that one.'”

He also revived the “voodoo penis” joke that he told at the 2018 Stand Up For Heroes event. It’s about a man who worries his wife will cheat on him while she’s out of town, so he buys her a “voodoo penis” that will magically go anywhere it’s asked.

“She realizes the husband didn’t tell her the word to turn off the voodoo penis,” Springsteen said. “After about 10 or 20 minutes, she’s had enough. She’s starting to get really nervous. ‘I gotta go to the hospital.’ She jumps in the car, hits the gas, she’s going 90 miles per hour in a 25-mile-per-hour zone. And she gets pulled over by a state trooper. He says, ‘License and registration.’ She says, ‘Officer, you don’t understand. A voodoo penis! A voodoo penis!’ He says, ‘Voodoo penis, my ass.'”

A joke about a sex shop worker selling a thermos to a woman requesting a plaid dildo was also familiar, though still delivered quite well. But the Western Stars songs were the clear highlight. In April 2019, Springsteen played the album in its entirety at a special concert in a barn on his New Jersey farm that was recorded for the Western Stars concert film and soundtrack. Last month, he sang “Stones,” “Hello Sunshine,” and “Moonlight Motel” during a private jam session at Danny Clinch’s Transparent Clinch Gallery in Asbury Park, New Jersey, on the same bill as Tom Morello, Dave Matthews, Jesse Malin, Daryl “DMC” McDaniels, and Taylor Momsen. But neither of those events was open to the public. entertainment.title: Messina Touring Group Looks To The Future: ‘As Things Are Changing, We Adapt’
entertainment.summary: The company's president of Nashville Haley McCollister reflects on Louis Messina's mentorship and belief in his staff.
entertainment.body:
The only job Haley McCollister has ever had has been at Messina Touring Group. Since joining the company’s ticketing department at 22 years old, she’s worked her way up and now serves as president of MTG’s Nashville office.

“The more he believed in me, the more I believed in myself,” McCollister says.

McCollister notes that many of her MTG colleagues have been with the company since they started their first jobs out of college. This is due to company founder Louis Messina ’s strong belief in each employee, with McCollister likening his support to how he strengthens his relationships with his artists.

Aside from McCollister, key members of the next generation at MTG include senior vp Sara Winter , vp of touring Keena Cheatham and vp Rachel Powers .

As the company continues to support its promoters, Messina has been passing more responsibilities onto his fellow teammates and providing them opportunities to foster their own artists. MTG maintains a small artist roster, wanting to provide all its attention to each client rather than having each person focus on multiple acts.

“We’re not out there chasing everything,” McCollister says. “To keep it this way, we have to grow very slowly. To find the ‘right’ artist for us to grow with starts with someone being extremely passionate about them and feeling it’s the right fit. And Louis is really supportive of us.”

McCollister and her colleagues fell in love with Phoebe Bridgers while she was opening for Taylor Swift on The Eras Tour and began discussions about bringing her into the fold. Messina came on board, and Bridgers is now promoted by MTG.

As the company looks ahead to its next quarter-­century, the team members feel they’re operating in a way they hope to be able to sustain.
