entertainment.body:
Jen Affleck is struggling after filing for divorce from her husband, Zac Affleck.

“It’s been really, really hard, but I’m trying my best to just stay positive,” the “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star — who is pregnant with with her fourth child — told Page Six’s “Virtual Reali-Tea” in a Zoom interview.

“My mindset is just what’s best for my kids and doing what’s best for them . There’s a lot to navigate.”

Jen — who is celebrating the release of Hulu’s “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County” spinoff— said divorce is “the hardest thing anyone can go through,” but knows filing was “what was best” for her family.

“I wouldn’t wish divorce on anyone,” she added. “Honestly, if you can avoid it, you should avoid it. All I can say is, I gave it my all.”

Jen, 27, filed for divorce from Zac, 30, last Tuesday, a mere 24 hours before they celebrated eldest daughter Nora’s 5th birthday together .

While details surrounding the split are currently under wraps, we confirmed Jen included a proposed co-parenting plan.

entertainment.body:
After filing for divorce from husband Zac Affleck , the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star shared insight into how she’s navigating her new normal.

“I'm not doing the best right now,” Jen— who is currently pregnant with her and Zac’s fourth baby—admitted to E! News in an exclusive interview. “I'm just taking one day at a time, and really just focusing on my kids. And obviously, the timing sucks, especially with me being pregnant.”

Nevertheless, she affirmed, “Ultimately, it was the best decision for us.”

And with that right decision bolstering her sails, Jen enjoyed sailing into the new horizon alongside her Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County costars Bobbi Althoff , Aspyn Ovard , Avery Woods , Madison Bontempo , McCall DaPron , Salomé Andrea , Ashleigh Pease and Jordan McClanahan .

For the Dancing With the Stars alum, the timing of filming Orange County made to an experience that was more freeing than her seasons on Secret Lives of Mormon Wives .

“What's funny is there was no reinventing this time,” the 27-year-old admitted. “I just showed up as me. I feel like for the past seven, eight years of my life, I've tried to mold myself into who I think people want to see, whether it be for my marriage or for TV or for the world. And this year was the first time that I really felt like I was reclaiming my identity and who I actually am.”

So, “going into the season, I just poured my heart into it,” she added. “Nothing was storyline; everything was real.”

That meant allowing the cameras to track her difficult chapter as it played out.

entertainment.title: Christina Applegate reveals surprising theory about what caused misdiagnosed MS symptoms
entertainment.summary: The "Dead to Me" star explained on her podcast that she's still desperately trying to find the cause of her debilitating health issues.
entertainment.body:
Christina Applegate thinks her breast implants may be the cause of her debilitating health issues.

“I had my double mastectomy in 2008 and I am way overdue for having them replaced,” she said on Tuesday’s episode of her “MeSsy” podcast.

“And I swear over the last five years or whatever, I’ve thought, ‘What if they’re leaking and poisoning me?'” the actress added.

Applegate, 54, told co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler “there’s some study” out there about leaked breast implants symptoms “presenting” as multiple sclerosis, which she was misdiagnosed with six years ago.

“So, that’s one that I will be looking into, because it’s something I’ve thought about,” she shared.

Applegate had a double mastectomy after she was diagnosed with breast cancer in August 2008.

Following the procedure, she underwent breast reconstruction surgery with saline expanders and subsequent saline implants.

In a 2009 interview with Women’s Health , Applegate admitted she missed her old boobs.

entertainment.title: Why Is Everyone So Mad at Supreme’s Elliott Smith Collaboration?
entertainment.summary: Elliott Smith’s music has been part of skate culture for decades, but for some reason a sweatshirt is being treated like a betrayal
entertainment.body:
Earlier this week, Supreme announced an Elliott Smith capsule collection, including a selection of jackets and T-shirts featuring artwork from across the late musician’s career, from his self-titled 1995 album to his seminal 1997 album Either/Or to 1998’s XO and 2000’s Figure 8 .

The internet seems to be in a huff over this, relying on a view of Supreme and streetwear frozen in 2008 that was, even then, embarrassingly myopic. The line of thinking goes that Supreme, the brand that was founded in New York in 1994 by designer James Jebbia and that has been a staple in skate and streetwear culture ever since, is an inauthentic purveyor of the ethos represented by Smith and his music. One might cite the brand’s roughly $500 million investment from the Carlyle Group in 2017 or its association with high fashion as disqualifying characteristics. More than anything, there seems to be a sense that taking shots at a nearly 40-year-old streetwear institution is a way to prove one’s unsullied dedication to a sense of anti-consumerism. The anger is misplaced.

In a culture awash in goofy collaborations and corporate cash grabs, Supreme might be one of the few brands still operating from an actual set of beliefs. Its Elliott Smith capsule (which was made with permission from Smith’s estate) is in a long line of collaborations that Supreme has done with musicians. Its first artist collaborator was Rammellzee, the experimental rapper and visual artist whose relationship with the brand dates to 1994 , the year Supreme opened. By 2005, Raekwon was posing with a Tickle Me Elmo for the first of Supreme’s commissioned portrait T-shirts . Across its music collaborations, portrait tees, and tributes, the list includes everyone from Michael Jackson to the Velvet Underground, Nirvana, Butthole Surfers, My Bloody Valentine, Daniel Johnston, Aphex Twin, and SALEM.

There have been collections with record labels like Stax , Wackies , Rap-A-Lot, Ruff Ryders , Jah Life, and Duck Down , the last of which put Black Moon and Smif-N-Wessun’s album artwork on clothes. There are shirts and shoes with Peter Saville’s artwork for Joy Division and New Order. The Smith collaboration is so patently in the wheelhouse of what the brand has done for decades that bringing it up now as some sort of “gotcha!” feels more like a product of social media’s tilt towards rage-bait than any defense of an artist. entertainment.title: Is the Hope at AFM Real?
entertainment.summary: Box office breakouts and a possible federal tax credit are lifting spirits among indie dealmakers — but disruption still reigns.
entertainment.body:
Film execs heading to L.A. for the American Film Market may be feeling something they haven’t in a while: hope.

Disruption still reigns, but independent and specialty fare has had a run of breakouts at the North American box office, topped by this weekend’s launch of Godzilla Minus Zero . The sequel from GKIDS and Toho opened to an estimated $32 million, well above the distributor’s mid-$20 millions projection. Takashi Yamazaki’s follow-up to the Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One (2023) reportedly cost in the mid-teens and is being touted as the biggest live-action foreign-language opening since 2004’s Hero , which bowed with $17.8 million. Related Stories Movies Brandon Sklenar on 'Iron Jane,' Body Dysmorphia and His Rapid Hollywood Rise Movies Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama 'I Is Another' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM

It isn’t the only surprise. A24’s You Can See Everything , the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, is entering blockbuster territory, having grossed almost $80 million domestically. That’s a rare result for nonfiction in a theatrical market that has been unkind to documentaries, and the film is only beginning to roll out internationally.

Niche programming is delivering, too. Angel Studios’ faith-based Drummer Boy , from directors Ben and Joel David Smallbone, opened to around $9 million. Nitesh Tiwari’s Indian epic Ramayana: Rise of a Legend , handled in the U.S. by Sony, grossed an estimated $8.6 million in its first weekend, on the widest domestic launch ever for an Indian film.

Add this year’s indie horror run, from Obsession ($500 million worldwide and counting) to Backrooms ($400 million-plus) and the self-distributed Iron Lung ($50 million-plus), and the makings of a good-vibes AFM are in place.

For sellers, the biggest takeaway is that audiences are showing up, and that they are young. Sarah Lebutsch, head of sales at U.K. group Protagonist Pictures, points to You Can See Everything as proof that a smart campaign and the right timing can still produce a hit. “Look at what You Can See Everything is doing at the moment in the U.S. It’s incredible,” she says.

She is equally encouraged by who is buying tickets. “It’s great to see those sorts of box office results, and the fact that Gen Z are going, and Gen Alpha are going and seeing films together in cinemas,” Lebutsch says. “There is a big resurgence of that, which I think we should all be very, very encouraged by.”

entertainment.title: MusiCares’ 2026 Wellness in Music Survey: 5 Statistics That Paint a Sobering Picture
entertainment.summary: The situation is even worse for emerging professionals (aged 18 to 24).
entertainment.body:
MusiCares shared key findings from its 2026 Wellness in Music Survey on Tuesday (Nov. 10), revealing that financial instability, limited access to healthcare and persistent mental health challenges remain closely interconnected across the music industry.

More than 3,300 music professionals responded to this year’s survey in English and Spanish, representing every U.S. state and Puerto Rico and more than 40 professions across the industry. The annual survey examines more than 100 indicators, including financial security, physical and mental health, access to health insurance and preventive care, substance use and confidence in sustaining a career in music.

MusiCares’ takeaway from the study: “Taken together, the 2026 findings point to a need for the industry to look beyond individual wellness interventions and more closely examine the underlying conditions affecting whether music professionals can build healthy, sustainable careers.”

This year’s survey also included dedicated outreach to emerging music professionals aged 18 to 24 with support from Live Free 999, a nonprofit founded by Carmela Wallace in honor of her son, the late rapper Juice WRLD , offering a closer look at the challenges facing the next generation entering the industry.

Since its founding in 1989, MusiCares has distributed more than $146 million in financial assistance to the music community. Findings from the Wellness in Music Survey help MusiCares identify where needs are most urgent.

In recent years, survey findings have helped shape expanded services, including access to women’s and family care through Maven Clinic, increased education around cannabis use, and scaled preventive care services. Following last year’s Wellness in Music data showing persistently high rates of suicidal ideation among music professionals, MusiCares also expanded its mental health resources through Tune Into Mental Health, developed with The Jed Foundation (JED) to provide mental health and suicide prevention resources tailored specifically to the music community.

B etween 46% and 50% of music professionals who responded to the survey earn less than $50,000 annually, while only 30% say they can comfortably cover their expenses through work in music. Finances remain the leading single source of stress, anxiety and depression across demographics.

entertainment.title: Rochelle Fleming, Singer With ‘Let No Man Put Asunder’ Disco Act First Choice Dies at 72
entertainment.summary: The vocalist passed away on Nov. 5 in her native Philadelphia.
entertainment.body:
Richelle Fleming-Finney, the co-founder and lead vocalist of Philadelphia disco soul group First Choice died on Nov. 5 at age 72. The news was announced on the singer’s Instagram page over the weekend in a message that read, “It is with a heavy heart to share the passing of, Rochelle Fleming-Finney. She was the founder of the R&B group, ‘First Choice.’ She passed away on November 5, 2026 at the age of 72 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.” Related Bella Kay Teases New Music In Billboard 'Up & Coming' Podcast Series Premiere: 'It's Kinda Giving Deluxe' It's Looking Like Oasis Will Skip Their Own Rock Hall of Fame Induction: 'It's Too Far To Be Going For the Night' Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Vince Gill, Halestorm & More Added As 2026 CMA Awards Performers Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

The memorial continued, “She bought light, laughter and love to the world. Services to celebrate her life will be announced at a later date. Thank you for your support during this difficult time.”

Fleming, who was born in Philadelphia on Feb. 11, 1954, formed her first vocal group in high school, the Debonettes, with fellow singers Annette Guest and Wardell Piper, later changing their name to First Choice while still students at Philly’s Overbrook High School. The budding dance soul group scored their first hit in 1973 with the early-disco burner “ Armed and Extremely Dangerous ,” which ran up to No. 11 on the Billboard R&B chart and No. 28 on the Billboard Hot 100 and had the hallmarks of the soon-to-explode genre, from syncopated bass to yearning vocals, a string section and a beat you could move your feet to.

Piper appeared on the group’s debut album, 1973’s Armed and Extremely Dangerous , but left shortly before its release, replaced by Joyce Jones on the LP that featured the funky workout and Billboard Hot 100 No. 56 hit “ Smarty Pants “; the album peaked at No. 184 on the Billboard 200 album chart. Following the addition of Jones, the group charted their first legit chart hit, the string-soaked No. 41 Hot 100 chart jam and title track from their sophomore release “The Player — Part 1,” about a no-good double-dealer who they warned would “Shoot you down/ Right down to the ground.”

Following Jones’ departure, after releasing two LPs on Philly Groove, the group jumped to Warner Bros. Records and released their third LP in 1976, So Let Us Entertain You , featuring such disco chart staples as “First Choice Theme/Ain’t He Bad” and “Are You Ready For Me?” The act scored a number of other hits in the mid-to-late ’70s, including Hot 100 No. 41 charting track “Doctor Love,” “Guilty” and “Let No Man Put Asunder,” which has been sampled on dance tracks and remixes from UGK, Liquid Crystal, Special Ed, 2Pac, House of Pain, Nitzer Ebb and many more, and was covered by Mary J. Blige on her 1999 Mary album.

entertainment.title: Thomas Markle court docs reveal truth about 82-year-old’s shocking mental decline amid child porn probe
entertainment.summary: A judge wrote in a two-page order that Meghan Markle's father should undergo a psychiatric assessment after his court appearance raised concern.
entertainment.body:
Thomas Markle will undergo a psychiatric evaluation to determine if he is mentally fit to stand trial on child porn charges .

On Friday, US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin in Tampa, Florida, wrote in a two-page order that the 82-year-old father of Meghan Markle should undergo a psychiatric assessment after his initial court appearance raised concern, per Reuters .

Griffin said in the court filing that she found “reasonable cause to believe” that Thomas may “suffer from a mental disease or defect rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense.”

The Florida-based judge said she based her findings on information provided about Thomas’ health condition, his “advanced age, and lack of recall.”

Forensic psychiatrist Dr. Amie Gerodimos has been ordered to conduct an independent psychiatric exam of Thomas to see if he can stand trial.

Dr. Gerodimos is slated to report back to the court on Nov. 20.

Last Friday, Thomas was arrested for possession of child porn in Florida, sources confirmed to The Post.

Page Six obtained images of Thomas — who got his leg amputated last year — being wheeled out of his nursing home while in handcuffs.

entertainment.title: Dustin Hoffman reveals pitiful salary he earned from blockbuster ‘The Graduate’ — admitting he had to go on unemployment after filming
entertainment.summary: Hoffman was embarrassed when Life magazine ran a photo of him at the unemployment office.
entertainment.body:
Dustin Hoffman was a huge star after “The Graduate” came out — but he was also broke.

The Oscar winner revealed in his memoir, “Look At Me,” that his life was “surreal” after the movie’s 1967 release.

“I couldn’t go out in the street without people coming up to touch me and ask for my autograph,” he wrote, “but I was still basically broke.”

The “Rain Man” actor, 89, said that he “only took home $3,000 after I paid all my expenses, believe it or not,” and even “had to pay my own way to L.A. for the shoot.”

When money ran out, Hoffman went on unemployment, but a photo of him at the unemployment office ran in Life magazine, “and I could never go back in there again. I was embarrassed by the dirty looks from other people standing in line who needed the money and assumed I didn’t.”

Hoffman also recalled having a “terrible” experience making the movie , largely because of director Mike Nichols, who he said became “an entirely different person” once filming began.

“The whole time, I felt Mike was angry at me, either because I was doing something wrong or because he had realized what everybody else already knew, that he had miscast the lead in his film,” he recalled.

“His mood would shift dramatically. I don’t remember the scene, but I will never forget Mike’s acid voice saying to me, after one take: ‘What were you doing?’ … Do the opposite of that.’”

entertainment.title: Josh Van Valkenburg Named President of UMPG Nashville, Troy Tomlinson to Shift Into Advisory Role
entertainment.summary: The leadership moves are expected to take effect as of Jan. 4, with Van Valkenburg reporting to UMPG chairman/CEO Jody Gerson.
entertainment.body:
Nashville music industry veteran Josh Van Valkenburg has been named president at Universal Music Publishing Group Nashville, Billboard has learned. Van Valkenburg, who will report to UMPG chairman/CEO Jody Gerson , will be based in Nashville and will assume the new role on Jan. 4, 2027.

Concurrently, longtime UMPG Nashville chairman/CEO Troy Tomlinson will transition to an exclusive advisory role supporting the company, its songwriters and its artists.

In his new position, Van Valkenburg will oversee the management and creative direction of UMPG Nashville, leading the company in identifying, signing and developing rising talent, while supporting its roster of songwriters, artists and producers. He will continue to deepen the company’s relationships throughout Nashville’s creative community, as well as expand opportunities for the company’s songwriters and catalogs.

Van Valkenburg most recently served as executive vp of creative at Sony Music Publishing Nashville. He was promoted to the role in 2021 and oversaw A&R strategy, songwriter development and creative opportunities for the company’s roster of songwriters and writer-artists. He has led Sony Music Publishing Nashville’s creative efforts since 2015 and previously served as senior vp of creative. Van Valkenburg began his music publishing career at EMI Music Publishing in 2006, joined its A&R team as creative manager in 2008, and became creative director at Sony/ATV in 2012.

“Country music is more global today than at any time in its history and the opportunities for Nashville’s songwriters have never been greater,” Gerson said in a statement. “Josh brings the vision, ambition and leadership skills to build on that momentum, along with deep relationships throughout the creative community and a gift for identifying and developing exceptional songwriters. I’m thrilled to welcome him to UMPG and look forward to all he and our Nashville team will accomplish together.”

During his career, Van Valkenburg has signed and been a champion for top songwriters including ASCAP songwriter of the year winner Josh Osborne , four-time BMI songwriter of the year winner Ross Copperman and SESAC songwriter of the year winner Jon Nite . Van Valkenburg has also championed hitmakers and award winners like Chris DeStefano , Natalie Hemby , Matt Rogers and Lindsay Rimes . He has also been involved in the careers of writers and artists including Ella Langley, Lainey Wilson, Thomas Rhett, Brett Eldredge, Charlie Worsham, Guy Clark and Johnnyswim. Van Valkenburg serves on the CMA board of directors and is an alumni advisor for Leadership Music.

entertainment.title: Doechii, T.I. & Yung Miami Lead 2027 Grammys Race for Best Rap Song and Performance: Our Predictions
entertainment.summary: From Yung Miami's anthemic "Spend Dat" to soul-stirring duets from Doechii and SZA, which rappers have the strongest chances at next year's ceremony?
entertainment.body:
From Drake’s jaw-dropping triple-album release to impressive stadium runs by Jay-Z and Ye , it’s been another busy year for hip-hop. Below, we assess the state of the three single-focused categories in the rap field at the 2027 Grammys : best rap performance, best rap song and best melodic rap performance.

Without an active Kendrick Lamar album cycle or competitive submissions from Drake or J. Cole, the Big Three will likely be absent from these three categories — at least as lead artists. That’s enough to clear the way for several frontrunners. For this category, Cardi B submitted “ErrTime,” which topped Rhythmic Airplay and hit No. 43 on the Billboard Hot 100 ; its quotable bars and Jeezy-esque flow should carry it into the final lineup of nominees. That all sounds easy enough, but given that Cardi’s sole best rap song nomination was for “Bodak Yellow” back in 2018, this is far from a done deal.

Female rappers have made solid inroads in this category throughout the 2020s, and Doechii and Yung Miami both have strong shots at nominations here. Already a two-time Grammy winner, Doechii is almost guaranteed to show up here with her SZA-assisted “Girl, Get Up.” That ruminative duet is a nice foil to Yung Miami’s “Spend Dat,” a New York Knicks-embraced summer anthem that soared to the top 20 of the Hot 100 (No. 17), an increasingly rare feat this decade for mainstream rappers not named Drake, Cardi B or Kendrick Lamar. Nonetheless, Lamar will be in contention here, thanks to his featured turn on Baby Keem’s “Good Flirts,” which also features Momo Boyd and has a solid chance of a nomination for best rap performance.

Male rappers also scored a handful of hits that could pop up in this category. Don Toliver is a frontrunner across the rap field, and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see “E85” nominated here. Likewise for Dave & Tems’ “Raindance” — a near-lock for a best melodic rap performance nod — and Lil Baby’s Pharrell-produced “Dead Fresh.” Near the top of the year, T.I. made an unexpected splash with his top 40 hit “Let ‘Em Know” (No. 33), and a nod in this category would be his fifth overall and first since 2010. He has never won. There’s also Belly Gang Kushington & 21 Savage’s “WTF Goin,” which dominated strip clubs, social media and urban radio in one fell swoop this year. 21 Savage’s sole Grammy win actually came in this category back in 2020 for his J. Cole-assisted “A Lot.” Don’t be too shocked to see him return with this runaway hit.

entertainment.body:
Wicker star Alexander Skarsgard will narrate Felled , the winning entry in a fan-fiction contest inspired by the world of Black Bear’s hit film, for audio erotica app Quinn , it was announced Tuesday.

Last month, ahead of the film’s theatrical release, Quinn partnered with Wicker to launch a fan-fiction contest inviting fans to create original stories set in the world of the film. With hundreds of submissions from around the world, Emma Parkinson’s Felled was selected as the winning entry. The story follows a willow tree that forms a deep attachment to a farmer’s daughter before being cut down. When they reunite years later, they discover that their bond has endured.

“I haven’t really experienced this before, where I’ve been part of a project that has taken on a life of its own like this,“ Skarsgard said in a statement. “It’s also been really fun and inspiring to see how creative people are.”

When asked what drew him to collaborate with Quinn, Skarsgard said, “It was quite refreshing to have something sensual and erotic that wasn’t androcentric for a change!”

“ Wicker fans have been so passionate about the film since day one, so partnering was a no-brainer,” says Caroline Spiegel, founder and CEO of Quinn. “There were hundreds of incredible, creative stories about mermen, porcelain men, witches and more. Felled stood out, and we knew our users had to hear Alexander narrate it.”

From directors, co-writers and real-life married couple Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, Black Bear’s Wicker has taken on a life of its own, going viral on social media and becoming an erotic, meme-making phenomenon.

The film, released on Oct. 23 and based on author Ursula Wills-Jones’s short story The Wicker Husband , follows “an ostracized fisherwoman ( Olivia Colman ) who commissions a husband made of wicker (Skarsgard) from the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). When her new husband awakens her desires and captures the village’s attention, jealousy, fascination and chaos follow, challenging the conventions of marriage, sex and the rules that bind them.“

entertainment.summary: Canadian director Rylan Oleksyn’s first feature centers on two young people with terminal cancer finding friendship and comic relief as they grapple with possible death.
entertainment.body:
Top Canadian singer-songwriter Jann Arden, Influencer star Cassandra Naud and Hunter Cardinal ( BET ) have nabbed lead roles in Expiry Date, a dark cancer dramedy from writer and director Rylan Oleksyn.

Naud plays Jessica and Cardinal is Milton, two young people living with terminal cancer. While initially clashing, they eventually find friendship and comic relief as they deal with family tensions and differing attitudes to treatment and possibly dying young. Arden, who along with Naud identifies as a queer artist, plays Jessica’s mother. “Jessica pushes Milton to take chances, while Milton helps Jessica confront what she has been avoiding. The film finds humor in their disagreements without losing sight of the circumstances that bring them together,” a synopsis from the producers states.

The film, director Oleksyn’s first feature that expands on an earlier short film of the same name, draws on the filmmaker’s experience in losing family members to a deadly disease. “Cancer has ripped holes in my family multiple times,” Oleksyn said in a statement. “With this film, I wanted to explore what these brave people can teach everyone who is lucky enough to stay healthy. I hope people will laugh, I hope people will cry, and I hope people will take it as a reminder of how quickly everything can go away, so go live.”

Arden, a multi-platinum recording artist and entertainer, as an actor co-created, executive produced and starred in the comedy Jann picked up by Hulu. Naud stars in Shudder ’s Influencer and the sequel Influencers , also appeared in Mike Flanagan’s Carrie series for Prime Video and has film and TV credits that include It’s a Wonderful Knife , opposite Joel McHale, and the series Tracker and Loudermilk.

Cardinal plays Michael in Netflix ’s BET live action TV adaptation of the hit Japanese manga thriller Kakegurui and has appeared in CBS’s Sheriff Country. He is also an indigenous artist and a veteran stage actor.

Expiry Date is shooting in Tisdale, Saskatchewan and is produced by Ryan Reaney and Kurtis Burke. Steven Gary Banks is executive producing.

“Working on Expiry Date is pretty kick ass. The entire town of Tisdale, Saskatchewan is behind Rylan and his crew. Great script, great actors, all coming together to make something wonderful,” Arden, a veteran of 16 studio albums and concert touring, said in a statement.

entertainment.title: Dua Lipa ‘Levitating’ Copyright Case Over ‘Talk Box’ Ends With Settlement
entertainment.summary: The agreement will finally resolve the last of several copyright lawsuits over Lipa's smash hit, which spent 77 weeks on the Hot 100.
entertainment.body:
The case, filed in 2023 by a producer named Bosko Kante , claimed that Lipa had paid to use his “talk box” recording in the original song, but had failed to secure his approval to use it in later remixes, like the even-more-popular version featuring DaBaby .

In court papers filed Monday (Nov. 9), attorneys for the two sides said they had reached an agreement to end the entire lawsuit permanently. The two sides had recently told the judge they were “discussing whether a potential resolution of this action is possible.”

Specifics of the agreement, such as monetary terms or whether credits on the songs would change, were not shared in court filings. Neither side’s lawyers immediately returned requests for more details or comment on the resolution of the case.

Monday’s settlement will finally end more than four years of continuous litigation over “Levitating,” Lipa’s breakout hit that reached No. 2 on the Hot 100 after debuting in 2020 and ultimately spent a whopping 77 weeks on the song chart.

In March 2022, a Florida reggae band called Artikal Sound System claimed Lipa stole the song’s core hook from their lesser-known 2017 tune “Live Your Life.” Days later, songwriters L. Russell Brown and Sandy Linzer accused Lipa of ripping off the melody from their disco tracks “Wiggle and Giggle All Night” and “Don Diablo.”

A year later, Kante filed his case centered on elements of the song created via talk box — a decades-old device that allows musicians to apply speech sounds onto the sounds of an instrument. After he contributed talk box clips to songs by Kanye West and Big Boi , Kante said a producer of “Levitating” reached out to ask him to add one to the upcoming song.

Kante said he reached an oral agreement that his materials could be used in “Levitating” but that the deal didn’t cover any further remixes — including the DaBaby remix and another version featuring Madonna and Missy Elliott .

Now, more than six years after “Levitating” was first released, the final pending lawsuit has been resolved via settlement.

entertainment.title: ‘Little Britain’ Star David Walliams Accused of Sexual Misconduct and Grooming
entertainment.summary: The comedian and best-selling author allegedly used his celebrity and star power to prey on women, according to a new report
entertainment.body:
British comedian and author David Walliams , best known for co-creating and starring in the sketch show Little Britain , has been accused of sexual misconduct by multiple women in a new investigation by The Guardian and ITV News .

The report featured accounts from over 30 people who accused Walliams of abusing his celebrity and star power to prey on women. While many women said they were over 18 when they had their alleged encounters with Walliams, some accused Walliams of first contacting them when they were teenagers.

Wallaims has been a prominent star in the United Kingdom for the past two decades, and was even appointed an officer of the Order of the British Empire by Queen Elizabeth II in 2017. He rose to fame with Little Britain , which ran for three seasons on the BBC between 2003 and 2006. Then, from 2012 to 2022, he was a popular judge on Britain’s Got Talent . Walliams was also a wildly successful author of novels and picture books for young adults and children, with his books selling tens of millions of copies worldwide.

Lawyers for Walliams denied the allegations against him, as well as any criminal wrongdoing. In a letter sent to The Guardian and ITV, Walliams said he sometimes “behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships” and “did not always take people’s feelings into proper account. That is something I regret.”

He continued: “And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did. I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

Walliams tried to stop the story’s release prior to publication by filing for a permanent injunction in U.K. court. He remained anonymous during the proceedings, referred to only as a ”well-known individual.” In arguing their case, Walliams’ lawyers said the comedian had attempted suicide over the summer after reporters first contacted him about the allegations. They suggested Walliams may attempt to harm himself again if the story was published. sports.title: Bengals call off trade for Arnold Ebiketie
sports.summary: Tuesday morning brought word that the Bengals had agreed to acquire pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie in a trade with the Eagles, but that agreement will not be finalized ahead of the 4 p.m.
sports.body:
Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the Bengals have called off the trade and will not be sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to Philadelphia.

The reports surfaced shortly after a tweet by OverTheCap.com contributor Nick Korte explained the compensatory pick ramifications of the deal . According to Korte, who focuses on the compensatory pick system, acquiring Ebiketie would put the Bengals in position to forfeit the third-round compensatory pick that they are currently set to receive for Trey Hendrickson leaving the team to sign with the Ravens.

That would greatly increase the price that the Bengals were going to pay to acquire Ebiketie and it appears they found it too high to move forward with the deal.

sports.title: Falcons signing K Jake Moody, releasing K Nick Folk
sports.summary: The Falcons are swapping out one kicker for another.
sports.body:
Atlanta is signing Jake Moody off of Baltimore’s practice squad and releasing Nick Folk, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.

Folk missed a field goal in two consecutive games and has made just 13-of-18 this season. He’s also missed an extra point, going 17-of-18 in the category in nine games.

With Tyler Loop on injured reserve, Moody was elevated from the practice squad and served as Baltimore’s kicker for Thursday’s loss to the Jaguars. He made a 53-yard field goal and an extra point.

Moody kicked for three different teams last season, finishing 19-of-23 on field goals and 15-of-16 on extra points.

Baltimore will need another kicker with Loop on IR for at least few more weeks.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have allowed 16 total points the past two games, but the unit has certainly faced lesser competition at quarterback. How much should we take from Buffalo’s recent defensive efforts? Is it all a mirage because they faced one snap of Lamar Jackson, only a few attempts from Tyler Huntley, then Joey Fagnano, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer? Or is Buffalo really onto something defensively? These type of questions are precisely why I created Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP). I introduced the new metric a few weeks ago, and if you missed that article, here’s how I can summarize DIP — it measures how well a defense performs against opposing quarterbacks relative to how those same quarterbacks perform against other defenses on their schedule. Pretty straightforward right? Baked into DIP is the exclusion of garbage time, and, like all EPA-based defensive stats, a negative figure is better. Also, quarterbacks need at least 30 attempts against other opponents to be counted toward a defense’s DIP. Buffalo’s unit made a steady climb after the first month or so of the season. It was 20th after Week 8 and 23rd through Week 6. And considering Buffalo’s current DIP placement, here’s where I land on what we can take from the club’s defensive efforts in Weeks 8 and 9 — for as much as the Bills defense was likely “helped” by low-level quarterback play these past two weeks it was close to equally as “hurt” by top-level quarterbacks it played in the first month-ish of the season. The analysis has to go both ways. And from that chart, you’ll notice that the DIP of the Bills defense is actually now into the negatives. That means, opposing pass games are actually performing slightly worse against the Bills than in their other games right now. sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk likely will be cut by 4:00 p.m. ET today
sports.summary: A key fact has come into focus regarding the Brandon Aiyuk situation.
sports.body:
Although it’s not clear how this happened (the Player Personnel Manual indicates that his 2025 salary of $1.17 million should have tolled into 2026 due to placement on the reserve/left squad list), official NFL records now show Aiyuk as having a base salary of $13.75 million for the balance of 2026. This means that, if he’s on the roster at the close of business on Tuesday, his salary for Week 10 vests — at $1.52 million.

They surely won’t be able to trade him at that number. And they surely don’t want to give him $1.52 million. Even more surely, coach Kyle Shanahan doesn’t want him in the building.

There’s still a story to be told as to the deal that was done to get the league to reinstate Aiyuk. The NFL and 49ers were putting the squeeze on Aiyuk to refund upwards of $13 million in previously-paid bonus money.

Our guess? Aiyuk wired a sizable payment to the 49ers (maybe $6 million or $7 million), the NFL reinstated him, and now Aiyuk will get his freedom.

sports.body: For a while Monday night, the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings seemed to be competing to see which offense could frustrate its fans the most. Neither team could get much going, and Josh Allen wasn’t doing much to hide his irritation. Playing without both his starting left tackle and left guard as Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson watched from the sidelines, Allen spent far too much time trying to escape a Minnesota defense that was coming through Buffalo’s offensive line like it had been invited. Fortunately, the Bills’ defense was giving the Vikings just as much trouble, and the scoreboard wasn’t moving much in either direction. But there’s only so long you can keep Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense quiet. Once Buffalo had a chance to figure out what Minnesota was throwing at them, the adjustments started paying off. It wasn’t the high-octane, 30-plus-point offense Bills fans have grown accustomed to watching, but it didn’t need to be. James Cook got rolling, Allen found a way to move the ball, and Tyler Bass quietly put together an 11-point night that deserves a little more attention. And let’s not forget fellow special-teams specialist Tommy Doman getting in on the tackling action. Because who doesn’t love seeing a punter-moonlighting-as-a-kicker make a tackle? By the time it was over, Buffalo had turned an aggravating start into a 23-6 win, improved to 7-1, and climbed to the top of the NFL standings. Not just the AFC East. Not just the AFC. All 32 teams. And while the offense was busy figuring things out, the defense was putting together another performance worth talking about. Three takeaways, fewer than 200 yards allowed, and a Minnesota offense that couldn’t convert a single third down. Of course, the win also came with a few entries in the record books. Josh Allen passed 5,000 career rushing yards and tied Peyton Manning’s mark of 322 total touchdowns through a player’s first 10 seasons. sports.title: Report: Dolphins DT Zach Sieler to have season-ending biceps surgery
sports.summary: The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season.
sports.body:
Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that defensive tackle Zach Sieler tore his biceps early in Sunday’s loss to the Lions. He was able to play the rest of the game, but needs to have surgery that will end his season.

Sieler started the first eight games of the season for the Dolphins. He had 24 tackles and two sacks in those appearances. He joined the team during the 2019 season and has 377 tackles, 37.5 sacks, two interceptions, five forced fumbles and six fumble recoveries during his time in Miami.

Sieler signed a three-year extension with the Dolphins ahead of the 2025 season. The deal ties him to the team through the 2029 season with cap hits of more than $20 million each year.

sports.title: Cardinals add QB Joey Aguilar off Jaguars' practice squad
sports.summary: After trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and then losing his replacement Gardner Minshew to a potentially season-ending elbow injury, the Cardinals are bringing in quarterback reinforcements.
sports.body:
Joey Aguilar will join the Cardinals’ 53-player roster from the Jaguars’ practice squad, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.

The 25-year-old Aguilar was the starting quarterback for the Tennessee Volunteers last season and spent a total of seven years in college football, with two at City College of San Francisco, two at Diablo Valley College and two at Appalachian State before transferring to Tennessee.

The only healthy quarterback in Arizona right now is rookie Carson Beck. Aguilar will presumably back him up on Sunday against the Rams, and the Cardinals will likely add another quarterback to their practice squad or active roster this week.

sports.title: The Vikings, as expected, are making calls about adding a quarterback
sports.summary: The clock is ticking, and it won't be cheap to trade for a starter.
sports.body:
They’re doing it today, in order to avoid having the season end at 6-11.

According to ESPNFL, the Vikings have begun making calls regarding a possible trade for a quarterback.

Of course they’re making calls. Coach Kevin O’Connell made that fairly clear last night. The real question is whether they can get a deal done.

They’re not operating from a position of strength, especially after a horrendous showing from Carson Wentz, whose passer rating against Buffalo was 8.9. The greater a team’s perceived need, the more the other team will want.

The Vikings’ best hope is to stumble into a situation where multiple teams are looking to unload a starter. By persuading one team that the Vikings will strike a deal with another team, the price could come down.

There aren’t many current starters who would even possibly be available. Two of them — Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones — have experience in Minnesota. Others include, potentially, Jets quarterback Geno Smith and Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.

Backups could be available. Mac Jones had been linked to Minnesota in the past. The 49ers would have to feel comfortable with the alternative to Mac Jones as the understudy to Brock Purdy. If a team trades its No. 2, it assumes the risk that the starter will get injured in the very next game.

That happened to the Steelers in 2019. They traded Josh Dobbs to the Jaguars after Nick Foles was injured in Week 1. In Week 2, the Steelers lost Ben Roethlisberger for the year. Then came the Duck Hodges show.

sports.title: Report: Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. at trade deadline
sports.summary: The Jaguars have been bringing players in to fortify the roster for a deep postseason run.
sports.body:
Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports the Jaguars plan to keep receiver Brian Thomas Jr. — barring a surprise.

Thomas has been rumored to be on the trade block largely due to his lack of production this season. He’s received just 22 targets in eight games, catching 10 passes for 117 yards with two touchdowns.

The No. 23 overall pick of the 2024 draft, Thomas caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards with 10 touchdowns as a rookie. But his production dipped even last year — the first season under head coach Liam Coen — with Thomas catching just 48 passes for 707 yards with two TDs.

Even with Fowler’s report, plans can change. If a team seriously needs a receiver and is willing to pony up, the Jaguars may change their mind about dealing Thomas before the 4 p.m. ET deadline.

sports.title: Jordan Davis is "a little disappointed" to be traded by Eagles
sports.summary: For players with no-trade clauses and most starting-level quarterbacks, there's no reason to worry about a rogue wind blowing them to a new team in a new city.
sports.body:
It happened on Monday to defensive tackle Jordan Davis. After the deal was done that sent him to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick, Davis commented on the situation.

“A little disappointed but, you know, understanding that they’re in the rebuilding process glad and you know, for the picks — first-round and second-round pick — obviously helps the team and, you know, I love those guys,” Davis told Jeff Skversky of Fox 29. “So however I can help the team, even in my departure, I’m absolutely glad to be doing that .”

He may or may not be glad for the likely uptick in his workload. In Philly, Davis was on the field for 52 percent of the snaps. Given what the Jaguars gave up for him, they’ll need more than that to justify the trade.

Either way, it’s part of life in the NFL. Even though the 32 businesses are independent, they’re branches of the same tree. An involuntary transfer is always a possibility for the vast majority of players.

sports.title: Jaguars trades for Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis could complicate deadline deals
sports.summary: It's Let's Make A Deal day in the NFL, with the window on trades closing at 4:00 p.m.
sports.body:
The Jaguars gave up a lot for two of the three players they acquired. As to safety Jessie Bates III, it was a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. For defensive tackle Jordan Davis (a run-stopper with 52-percent playing time), it was a first-round pick and a second-round pick.

Those deals will hover over today’s talks. Teams that are considering trading players will, at some level, be concerned about the perception that they didn’t get enough, relative to what the Jaguars invested on Monday.

If the Jaguars intended that, they’re next-level super geniuses. Go all in, acquire players who’ll help the team get to the Super Bowl and win it, and make it harder for other contenders to do the same thing today.

As it relates to Jacksonville receiver Brian Thomas Jr., a first-round pick in 2024 who had 1,282 yards as a rookie and doesn’t fit the current offense, that could also result in a better haul, if/when the Rams join the effort (which includes the Chiefs, Steelers, and Commanders) to wrest Thomas away from the Jaguars.

Regardless of the motivation(s), Monday’s trades by the Jaguars could make it harder for deals to get done on Tuesday. Most notably, it could make the Colts decide not to take the best offer on the table for running back Jonathan Taylor.

With the Giants offering a two and a five, would the Colts be willing to accept for Taylor what the Jaguars gave up for Bates? How much more will it take to get the Colts to believe it’s a proper return given the investment made in getting Bates?

However it plays out, if not much happens at the deadline, the wrench thrown into the gears by the Jaguars could be a factor in that.

sports.title: Klint Kubiak: We wouldn't be where we are without Kirk Cousins' "amazing" decision-making
sports.summary: The Raiders signed Kirk Cousins in April with the idea that he would start for the entire season while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza develops.
sports.body:
That plan has had solid returns, with Cousins completing 64.1 percent of his passes for 2,340 yards with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions.

But three of those picks came in Sunday’s loss to the 49ers, which was Cousins’ worst game of the season. On Monday, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the QB’s decision-making on the giveaways.

“Kirk has been an extremely solid decision maker all season,” Kubiak said, via transcript from the team. “There’s ones he wants back. He wants back the first play of [the] second half. [He] wants back the one in the red zone where we did not give him protection to make a good decision. In the last play of the game, we’re trying to make a play, so he wants those back.

“But we’re not in the position that we are without the amazing decisions he’s made all year. So, we’ve got to coach up those ones and help him learn from them. But again, I’m very pleased with — the quarterback has to be the best decision-maker on the team, any organization. He wasn’t on those two plays, and that last one I’m calling a heave-ho.”

With the trade deadline rapidly approaching and the Raiders sitting at 4-5, there have been rumors about teams being interested in Cousins. Kubiak was asked how he thinks players like Cousins and Maxx Crosby — who expressed no interest in being traded — are handling that situation.

“Well, that’s the business that we’re in,” Kubiak said. “That’s the business of football, and those guys are veterans. They’ve been around that, so you just keep working. There’s a lot of things that are out of your control.”

If the Raiders were to trade Cousins, it would signal that the team feels Mendoza is ready to take over as starting quarterback. But because Las Vegas is still in the thick of things in the AFC as the current No. 9 seed, they may not be inclined to shake things up at the game’s most important position.

sports.title: Jerry Jones doesn't expect a "significant trade" for Cowboys on Tuesday
sports.summary: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has said repeatedly that he's open for business on the trade front, but every deal needs a partner and it doesn't sound like the Cowboys are finding much luck on that front.
sports.body:
The trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday and Jones is heading toward that hour with low expectations for major changes to the roster.

“You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling ,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan. “It’s really not ringing, which you’ve heard me say numerous times — that’s when you make a trade. Don’t count it out. A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”

Jones did say that the team will make a move to address running back after losing Tyler Goodson to a knee injury, but he said he thinks that move is more likely to involve signing someone from outside the organization than it is to come via a trade.

sports.title: Tom Brady sells stake in Birmingham City Football Club
sports.summary: Tom Brady has a lot on his plate (but not any deli meat).
sports.body:
The Birmingham City Football Club has announced that Brady has exited the franchise.

“Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the Club over the last three years,” the team said in a website post with the headline “ Tom Brady Departure .”

Brady acquired a minority share in the team, and became chairman of the advisory board, in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL.

Brady, whose other gigs include serving as Fox’s top NFL analyst and owning a piece of the Raiders, made waves with comments made in a Birmingham City documentary (or, as most sports documentaries now are, an infomercial) regarding the work ethic of former club manager Wayne Rooney.

There’s no reason to ever question Brady’s work ethic. There are plenty of reasons to question whether he tries to do too much by wearing so many hats. There are only so many hours in the day, only so many days in the week.

If, along the way, he got a nice return on his investment, even better for Brady. Especially since he seems to be in a race with Peyton Manning to acquire enough money to become the controlling owner of an NFL team.

The biggest problem is this. As Brady’s net worth grows, the price tag for NFL ownership grows even faster.

Regardless, he likely now has more cash to add to the fund for potentially purchasing a franchise and, more importantly, one less thing to consume his time and attention.

sports.title: Dan Campbell on benching Christian Mahogany: That's why I have team rules
sports.summary: Lions guard Christian Mahogany had played every snap for five consecutive games until Sunday in Miami, when Mahogany didn't play at all and backup Miles Frazier took his place.
sports.body:
Campbell didn’t get into specifics about which rules Mahogany violated, but he said that even though the offensive line was struggling without Mahogany early in Sunday’s win over the Dolphins, he never wavered in his belief that a player who hasn’t been meeting expectations isn’t going to play.

“Frazier earned that opportunity, and I thought he got better as the game went on, and you could say that about the whole unit — we were a little shaky early,” Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket .

Campbell said he won’t talk publicly about what Mahogany did to earn the benching, but he did say Mahogany had broken a team rule more than once.

“That’s really between us,” Campbell said. “That’s why I have team rules, that’s why we have team rules and we’ve all got to abide by them, and if it’s broken multiple times, then you do something about it. We’re in good standing and like I said, the ball’s in his court. It’ll be good.”

Campbell said Mahogany respects his decision, and that the whole team needs to understand that the head coach is going to hold every player to a high standard.

“Listen, we’re good. He knows. We’re all good. He’ll be fine,” Campbell said. “Look, if you say you’re going to do something, you better hold up to it or otherwise you’re going to lose the respect of people around you. Because if I’m sitting in that seat and I say one thing and then I don’t do it, I’ll immediately lose respect for that person. So we stick by what we say we’re going to do here.”

sports.body: James Cook has moved ahead of Josh Allen on the Buffalo Bills’ all-time rushing list, taking over fourth place in franchise history during Monday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings Cook entered the game with 4,966 career rushing yards, just 25 behind Allen’s 4,991. Cook needed to outgain his quarterback by at least 26 yards to move into fourth place, but it wasn’t quite that simple. Allen had 60 minutes to add to his total as well. Cook added 107 yards Monday night to bring his career total to 5073. Allen added just 15 and now has 5006. Interestingly, the pair are the first teammates in NFL history to join the 5k-Club on the same night. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2119996353845891089?a=hmXQbUmS10zkGgMclg4&s=20] Cook now trails only Thurman Thomas (11,938), O.J. Simpson (10,183), and Fred Jackson (5,646) on Buffalo’s all-time rushing list. With nine games remaining in the regular season, Cook also has a shot at catching Jackson for third place in 2026. With 573 separating the two, Cook would need to average just over 63 yards per game over the remaining nine games to move up another spot before the season ends. Of course, Allen isn’t going to stop running the ball either, so Cook may have to defend his new spot on the list a few times. The move up the franchise leaderboard comes just a few weeks after Cook passed Joe Cribbs for fifth place during Buffalo’s game against the Detroit Lions. Cook moved ahead of Cribbs’ 4,445 career rushing yards with a 22-yard run in the fourth quarter, continuing his climb through a list that includes some of the biggest names in Bills history. Cook has been making up ground on Allen throughout the season, but the gap narrowed considerably in Buffalo’s Week 6 game. Cook rushed for 95 yards against the Las Vegas Raiders, while Allen finished with just 1. That performance cut Allen’s lead from 169 yards to 75. The two players have taken very different paths to their places on the list. Cook, now in his fifth NFL season, has become the centerpiece of Buffalo’s running game, while Allen has built his rushing total as one of the league’s most dangerous dual-threat quarterbacks. Allen also holds the NFL record for rushing touchdowns by a quarterback.

“This one felt pretty terrible. I’m not going to lie,” Wentz said, via the Associated Press.

sports.title: Kevin O'Connell on potential quarterback trade: "I'll defer to Nolan [Teasley] on that"
sports.summary: Vikings coach doesn't rule out making a deal by Tuesday's deadline.
sports.body:
“I’ll defer to [G.M.] Nolan [Teasley] on that,” O’Connell said. “We’ve had dialogue about a lot of different positions. And tight turnaround obviously playing the Monday night game before that, and we’ll get right to work on any potential moves that can be there. But really just focused on the game tonight, which was not good enough in any way, shape, or form.”

O’Connell was asked at one point whether he has ever felt as challenging as it does right now, as a play-caller.

They have options. Several teams could be looking to make a deal. And even if it won’t be cheap, it’s necessary to salvage what was, only nine days ago, a very promising season.

It still can be. A return of Kirk Cousins would be a B-12 shot to the franchise. Even Daniel Jones would make things better than they are.

And if they want to go all in, try to make a deal for Justin Herbert — who may be thrilled at this point to don an eye patch and escape from L.A.

Whatever the Vikings do, they need to do something. Otherwise, there may not be a quarterback change when the season ends.

sports.title: Receiver-needy teams should call about Justin Jefferson
sports.summary: If the Vikings aren't going to upgrade at QB, they should give Jefferson a chance at a championship.
sports.body:
Few players are untouchable, when it comes to a trade. And even if the Vikings would hang up the phone and not listen, teams that need a high-end pass-catcher should try.

The Rams currently are in a pickle, thanks to the placement of Puka Nacua on injured reserve, where he joins Davante Adams. The Chiefs could use help at the position, too.

Ditto for the Steelers, who (like the Chiefs and Commanders) have interest in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

Then there are the 49ers, who are always lurking when it comes to possibly making a big move.

Regardless, it makes sense to make the call. If the Vikings aren’t going to make a move for a functional quarterback, they should stockpile picks and give Jefferson a chance to chase the championship that won’t happen in Minnesota — especially if they waste his seventh season by not upgrading at the quarterback position.

Yes, a trade would come with a 2027 cap charge. The Vikings also would avoid the $30 million he’s due to make in 2027, and the upgrade to meet the increased market that he surely already wants.

At the end of the day, it’s one or the other. Trade for a better quarterback, or trade Jefferson to another team. Of the available options, doing neither makes the least sense.

sports.body: ESPN named James Cook the player of the game in their postgame show and it’s easy to see why. The Buffalo Bills leaned on their running back against the Minnesota Vikings, and despite a slow start, Cook delivered over the course of the game and scored what felt like the game-ending touchdown with 6:17 left in the fourth quarter. That’s seven straight games with a rushing touchdown for Cook. He also has 75+ rushing yards in those games, the longest streak in team history with 75 yards and a touchdown run. That combo is the longest streak by a player since 2006 when LaDanian Tomlinson had eight straight. Cook’s previous career high in carries came in 2025 when he ran the ball 32 times with two offensive lineman injured against a really talented Pittsburgh Steelers defense. The same thing happened in Minnesota, when two Bills offensive linemen were on the shelf and Buffalo needed the help. Cook toted the rock 31 times for 107 yards at a tough 3.5 yards per carry. Cook’s long was only 11 yards on Monday. In the passing game, Cook was targeted once but let the Allen pass go through his hands but he probably wouldn’t have picked up many yards anyway. The rest of the rushing game was shaky at best. Josh Allen ran the ball five times for 16 yards (outside the first half kneel down), mostly on designed runs. Ray Davis had two runs for two yards. Ty Johnson had one rush for one yard. There was some consternation about signing Cook to his current contract a while ago, but that seems to have passed. Cook deserves a ton of credit for continuing to grind against the Vikings. It’s a short week for the Blls heading into a Sunday game after a road trip on Monday night, so hopefully he can get iced up with a veteran rest day this week. After the game, Cook was nonchalant on how his body feels. “[I feel] excellent. Feel like I didn’t play a game.” Hopefully he feels that way in the morning.

sports.summary: Failure to act leads to one conclusion: The Vikings are dysfunctional.
sports.body:
What will they do about a team with a Super Bowl-caliber defense and an offense that could barely function in the MAC?

The window remains open until 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday. The Vikings were in this spot three years ago, when Kirk Cousins tore an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline.

That time, the Vikings didn’t have many options; they ended up with Josh Dobbs. This time, there are two former Vikings on other teams who know the Minnesota offense: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins.

If the calls haven’t already been made, they should be. Immediately. What will it take to salvage a season that is disintegrating before everyone’s eyes, despite the 6-2 record?

It wouldn’t be easy to plug and play a new quarterback, but there’s history with Jones and Cousins. It would be easier to get them up to speed than if they brought in someone who would be learning everything from scratch.

If, in the end, the Colts want too much for Jones and the Raiders want too much for Cousins (neither is untouchable; the question is the amount of the compensation), the only other starter potentially available would be Geno Smith.

Some have suggested a play for Justin Herbert. At this point, however, it’s impossible to know whether his implosion is about his surroundings or about Herbert.

Then there’s Jimmy Garoppolo, who remains a free agent — and who has been largely forgotten.

sports.title: Sean McVay on Puka Nacua injury: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't questioning that play call
sports.summary: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders.
sports.body:
Nacua’s injuries occurred on the Rams’ final offensive play when he was tackled after rushing for five yards on third-and-11. Nacua took a handoff on the play and head coach Sean McVay was asked at a Monday press conference if he second-guessed himself for putting Nacua in position to take a hit at that point in the game.

McVay said he’s “kicking myself about those kinds of things” and called it something the Rams have to think about “internally” as they move forward.

“I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion, and maybe ended the game that would’ve led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee,” McVay said. “It’s stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we’ve got to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine. He’s a guy we have to be intentional about because it’s a bummer. Because he can do so much, you want to make sure you don’t take that for granted.”

With Nacua and Davante Adams now out for the indefinite future, the Rams may be in the market for receiving help before the trade deadline passes at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. They do not have their 2027 first- or third-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick or their 2029 third-round pick thanks to their trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie.

sports.title: Eagles say Jaguars made an offer they couldn't refuse for Jordan Davis

sports.body:
The Jaguars are sending a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles.

“We are extremely grateful to Jordan for his contributions to our team on the field and in the Philadelphia community since we drafted him five years ago,” the team said in a statement. “He has been a key contributor to our team culture and on-field success, which included two Super Bowl appearances and a world championship in 2024. His growth and development as both a player and a leader are a testament to his hard work and character. We wish Jordan nothing but continued success.”

The Eagles now have first-round picks in the 2027 draft, two first-round picks and two second-round picks in the 2028 draft and multiple second-round picks in 2029.

The Eagles made Davis a first-round pick in 2022, and he totaled 193 tackles, 9.5 sacks, 15 quarterback hits and 11 passes defensed in 73 games.

sports.title: NFL reinstates WR Brandon Aiyuk from reserve/left squad list
sports.summary: 49ers' get a two-week roster exemption.
sports.body:
The NFL reinstated the 49ers receiver from the reserve/left squad list on Monday. The league also gave the 49ers a two-week roster exemption, giving the team a window for making a decision about what to do with Aiyuk.

The 49ers now have an immediate decision to make about Aiyuk. If he’s on the roster on Tuesday at 4:00 p.m. ET, he’s owed a game check for the week.

Based on the Player Personnel Manual, placement on the reserve/left squad list apparently tolled his 2025 salary. That means he’ll return to the $1.17 million base salary from 2025, with the 2026 salary of $26.015 million delayed until 2027.

It gives the 49ers a window to trade Aiyuk, with the new team getting him for the rest of the season at only $585,000 in non-guaranteed pay.

The 49ers can carry Aiyuk as an extra man on the roster until Monday, November 23.

It’s unclear, currently, whether Aiyuk agreed to refund past bonus money to the 49ers in order to get the league to reinstate him. If the 49ers trade or release Aiyuk, the 49ers lose the ability to get money back from Aiyuk.

sports.title: Todd Monken not ready to name starter at QB for Week 10
sports.summary: Shedeur Sanders has given Todd Monken something to think about.
sports.body:
The Browns’ head coach told reporters in his Monday news conference that he’s not ready to name a starter at quarterback for the Week 10 matchup against the Texans.

That came after Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reported that Deshaun Watson would be back in the saddle after missing Sunday’s game.

“I really haven’t thought through it other than getting through this morning’s tape,” Monken said. “I just got done meeting with the guys. They’ll flush the game and then we’ll have a chance to meet offensively more [extensively] later today. We went through the tape, immediately had to break, go to personnel, then the team comes in, and we haven’t had a chance to circle back as an offensive staff.”

Watson started the first eight games of the season for Cleveland, generating five game-winning drives for the team’s five wins.

Sanders, who started after Watson missed the first two days of the practice week while in concussion protocol, completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards with two touchdowns and no picks against the Saints.

“Well I’m awfully proud of him ,” Monken said of Sanders. “It’s been 10 weeks since he had reps with the ones. I think it showed up, the reps that we gave him in camp.

“I thought he battled. I thought he showed composure in the pocket, getting to his check-downs at times. He made plays with his feet in escaping. He made the scramble play to Jerry [Jeudy]. He made a big third-down conversion early and he made one right there in four-minute, right before the holding call that gave us a first down. So, that’s what you wanted to see.”

Monken noted that philosophically, he doesn’t really think of a player losing a job due to injury.

sports.title: Jesse Minter does not address Lamar Jackson's injury, says he'll keep conversations with QB private
sports.summary: Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026.
sports.body:
Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, however, was not inclined to give any update on the star QB in his Monday press conference.

Jackson is reportedly out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb. He is currently on injured reserve.

Minter was asked what the chance is that Jackson will be able to return this season.

“You know, I’m going to keep most of the conversations between Lamar and I between Lamar and I ,” Minter said. “Again, just like before, it’s a guy when you’re dealing with something, that no one wants to be on the field more. He’s probably going to do everything he can to put himself in position [to play]. But I’ll leave it at that.”

Minter also did not say whether or not Jackson requires or already has had surgery.

“I’m going to keep all that stuff between me and him,” Minter said.

Does that mean the public won’t know the nature of Jackson’s injury and if he can return?

There was one more follow-up in the press conference, with Minter being asked if it’s accurate to say Jackson’s thumb was fractured and dislocated.

sports.title: Jets trade defensive back for 2028 draft pick
sports.summary: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a […]
sports.body: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth round draft pick. That’s better. The Jets originally acquired Andre Cisco by signing him as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. Cisco was brought in expecting to be a playmaker in the back end of the defense, but it did not work out that way. After eight weeks of uninspired play in 2025 in which Cisco racked up zero interceptions, one pass defended, one tackle for loss and one fumble recovery, with little in the way of defensive playmaking, Cisco’s 2025 campaign ended with a season ending injury. The Jets let his contract expire in 2026 and Cisco explored free agency before the Jets brought him back on a one year, $2.2 million deal. He was expected to compete with Dane Belton for the safety spot opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick, but Belton is clearly the better player. Fitzpatrick missed time early in the season, opening up playing time for Cisco, but Cisco did little with the opportunity. Once Fitzpatrick returned to action Cisco was relegated primarily to special teams play. Over parts of two seasons Andre Cisco played 17 games for the Jets, starting 12. He racked up a total of 64 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, one forced fumble, three tackles for loss and one fumble recovery with the Jets. Cisco allowed an abysmal 115 passer rating in coverage during his time with the Jets. The trade of Cisco opens up playing time for 2025 fourth round draft pick Malachi Moore in the short run. 2026 seventh round pick V.J. Payne also stands to benefit from the trade as he works his way back from a preseason injury that has kept him out of action so far this season.

“Patrick, he is really day-to-day right now ,” head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Monday news conference. “It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. sports.body: Over the last several weeks, we have seen the classic unraveling of a Jets season. The faces change, but the results always seem to stay the same. Entering Week 7, the Jets faced a two game homestand against beatable opponents. Victories against both the Dolphins and the Raiders would get the team to .500 through eight games and give this team real momentum heading into a tough stretch facing the Chiefs and Bills back-to-back. Of course, the Jets handed the previously winless Dolphins their first victory and then lost to the Raiders, dropping their record to 2-6. Not even at the halfway point, the season was over. It is normal for the competitive portion of the season to end early for Jets fans. It feels like an annual tradition in November to be discussing NFL Draft position above all else. The only thing the Jets still had going for them is it felt like the team was still united. Players were fighting for each other. Things changed in the Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The Jets looked like an imploding team. Fans could see it in obvious ways like Minkah Fitzpatrick making a couple of business decisions when he had opportunities to make plays. Armand Membou threw his helmet in frustration in an emotional outburst after allow a second half sack. Geno Smith was demonstrative in his frustration frequently as the game slipped away. These are symptoms of a season that is slipping away and a team that is in a spiral. Through each offseason NFL fans of all 32 teams convince themselves that their team has made all of the right moves, and their roster is improved. That’s part of being a fan. At this time of year, Jets fans frequently are forced to confront the reality that the team made bad moves in the previous offseason, and that has a lot to do with the team’s struggles. The Jets might not have gotten everything wrong in the 2026 offseason. David Bailey increasingly looks like a budding star. If the two pass catchers the Jets took in the first round of the NFL Draft after Bailey aren’t dominating, they at least look promising. Still, at this point I think the obvious is staring Jets fans in the face. sports.body: The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 - 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 - 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook. Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Regardless, if the Jets don’t exit next week with their eighth loss of the season it will be a major surprise. --- Join Gang Green Nation on game day! sports.title: Nick Sirianni: We'll talk about possible staff changes during bye week
sports.summary: The Eagles lost their seventh straight game on Sunday and they'll head into their bye week with little hope of salvaging anything over their final eight regular season games.
sports.body:
That’s shifted the focus in Philadelphia to what kinds of changes may be coming for the team. Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked if there’s any chance of those changes starting with alterations to the coaching staff during the week off.

“We’ll talk. Obviously, right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything,” Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. “I think we always think — we’ll do everything. I’ll do anything I can to help this team win football games. Like I said, I’ll look at myself internally first and then go from there. My job is to coach the players and to coach the coaches, and anything I can do to help this team win games, we’ll do. Everything can always be on the table, but I don’t think you change just to change because that’s what your record says that -- you’ve got to look at what’s really real and not react to anything else. Again, I just don’t believe you just change just to change. If you have a strong reason to do things in anything, not just change, but in anything and you’re convicted on it, that’s how we’ll go about our business.”

Sirianni faced further questions about offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and changes on that side of the ball, but Sirianni said he was “not going to get into the hypotheticals” while reiterating that he’s willing to do anything he can to make the team better. The coming days should bring more word about whether any of that will involve changes to his staff.
